title: Am I justified in thinking this was assualt?
body:
Alright so for context, I'm a dude but a trans one. I'm out fully, have been for years, everyone treats me like a guy, I'm known as a guy at uni, I make sure that I "act" and look like a guy (sometimes to the expense of my own personality lol) so basically in all contexts everyone sees me as one including all my (now ex) flatmates. This included one of my flatmares,  I'll call him Lewis, who up until January saw me as a dude and we were just mates. I actually was pretty stoked to have him as a friend and i thought he was awesome. Then around Jan he starts out of literally no where misgendering me whereas he hadn't before. It started off as jokes like we were joking about being old and he called me a old granny but I didn't really take it personally at that point. But then he straight up starting treating me like a woman. he's introduced me as a girl, he'd use the wrong pronouns, he found out my old name from my bank card (I told him not to look) and starting boasting about it. Also around this time, he started making "jokes" about us dating and the most painfully awkward one was that we went to go get burritos and he said, all seriousness "this is a nice little date we're on" and I just kinda died of the cringe and gave him a little bit of a cold shoulder for the next few days but then I just kinda let it go. 

Fast forward to March, Me, Lewis and my friend Ann went clubbing and we all drunk having a good time just literally being mates. Not once did I say ANYTHING flirty or anything we were just goofing around it was fun. Then at some point during the night, Ann goes to the bathroom and me and Lewis sit at a booth. We are talking about, again nothing flirty, just literally laughing about something that happened that night he starts rubbing his hand across my thigh and I just freeze. Its so dumb because I probably could have told him to stop but I didn't for some reason I just froze. And he didnt really touch me anywhere super weird but he did like squeeze my inner thigh which just made me feel a bit gross to be honest. He stopped eventually, or I think I made some move to angle myself away from him and honestly for the rest of the night I just consciously forgot about it. But the days following I felt horrible, then I convinced myself it wasn't a big deal but as time went on I was just so mad about it cause I figured he had started to misgender me and stuff because he suddenly starting liking me but isnt comfortable of the idea of getting with a guy ( I don't even think be liked me tbh, he talks ALL THE TIME about how he can never get women and he just figured he'd try me cause I was there essentially) 

I was mad about it cause it made things awkward and I felt so bit used but I didn't really think it was assualt as such until I heard through the grapevine that he has a bit of a pattern of being creepy around women when he's drunk and now I'm thinking about how scared I was during it (that might be dumb) and I keep going to be like "oh this wasn't assault it wasn't that bad" but if any of my friends ever told me a similar story, I'd probably say it's assualt but I'm so anxious about this now. I keep thinking about it, I'm scared cause I gotta see him at campus when I go back to uni and honestly I'm just feeling super shitty about this. 


Sorry this is so long, I haven't really talked about this in front of anyone and I can't really say I've been assualted (if it's that) and I know it wanst that bad but this whole thing is making me so gross and horrible.
parent_comment: yeah i’m not sure if the thigh incident is considered SA legally (it might be i’m not sure), but it sounds like if you hadn’t taken distance away from this person something bad could’ve happened, and it’s okay to feel gross about what happened. i am a cis woman, so it’s very different but imagine if someone just started referring to me as a man and sexualizing me as a gender i’m not? doesn’t make any sense. super sorry again and maybe try therapy if u can !!

title: I don't understand why I kept seeing my abuser for so long.
body:
So, I was sexually assaulted and raped multiple times by a former friend of mine. His girlfriend used to invite me over and I felt like I couldn't say no to her because of what was happening with her boyfriend -I was feeling guilty and ashamed, even though I wasn't even interested in him and had expressed my disinterest to him already.

I didn't consent to her boyfriend sending me very explicit text messages as well as very explicit pictures. He pressured me into giving him oral and I eventually gave in because it was too much for me and me saying "No." never even worked anyway.

Now, the thing is, this lasted for months. His girlfriend would invite me over on weekends and almost every weekend, the same cycle would repeat itself. She would go to bed early and I would find myself alone with her boyfriend. That's when it mostly happened.

I have a hard time defining consent because I have a very hard time saying no. I'm a people pleaser but I'm working on improving myself for my own safety.
I just feel so stupid because I kept coming over to their house only because I felt like I couldn't say no to either of them. The girlfriend was going through a tough time and I wanted to be here for her as much as I could but it also meant I had to endure assaults and rapes almost every weekend during ten months from her boyfriend.

In a way, I was almost "scared" he would stop doing these horrible things to me because I knew that once it would end, it meant that I would have to realize he had indeed assaulted and raped me and I didn't want to be a victim. I didn't even feel like one for a long time until it took a toll on my mental health and well-being.

I don't know if anyone has figured it out yet but why do victims stay or come back to their abusers?

I know there were countless of ways I could have put an end to that -and I eventually did and even reported him to the police- but I wish I had done it sooner...
parent_comment:
similar sitch - one of my abusers was my childhood best friend, he assaulted me many times all through hs, just gently "pushing" the envelope - harassing me, groping me, and commenting about my body. he later actually drugged and raped me. 

tldr; I also asked myself why I stuck around for so long - part of it was shock and not knowing what to do, another part was not wanting to believe someone I trusted would do this to me.

title: Coming to Terms
body:
A couple of years ago, I was dating this guy. We had such a great texting relationship. Talked everyday, all day. I liked the person he was over the phone. But, I had this feeling that something was off. In person, it was different. He was more quiet and it felt awkward but I just thought maybe he is shy? After we would hang out for a little bit, he would want to start hooking up. I was okay with it but thought it was kind of odd? I have not had a lot of sexual experiences and if I did, it was someone I was dating or in a serious relationship with. When we would hang out, I kept wondering why couldn’t we just talk and if it mutually leads to that then okay? But it felt like it wasn’t 30 minutes into us hanging out, he was tryin
g to make out. He was always the initiator. Keep in mind, we only ever went to one public outing. The rest was always at my place or his. He definitely strung me along and I was low on his priority list. But, at the time, I had little to no self worth. I thought I deserved it or I could make excuses for it. I didn’t feel confident in the relationship. He started becoming more distant and I kept holding on. Thinking maybe it could work. But I still had that feeling that something was off. That this isn’t what a relationship should be. I was too insecure at the time to trust myself. 

We were suppose to hang out the day after thanksgiving. An hour before, he tried to bail. He wanted to go hang with his cousins. I was crushed. Then, he said I could come over to hang out before he left. Deep down, I knew better but I still went over. He was leaving crumbs and I was taking them. When I got over, none of his roommates where there so I thought we would hang out in the living room. Nope. He took me straight upstairs to his room. We were laying on his bed and I was trying to make small talk. I thought we could watch a movie. He wasn’t saying much. But just enough to keep me there. I felt uncomfortable but thought I was overreacting. He started making out with me. Not romantic at all like he was getting what was “his”. It felt kind of forced. I went along with it. I loved to makeout and it wasn’t unusual but I felt that this time it was different. Clothes started to come off. But, I didn’t want to do more than that. I wanted to actually hang out with him and get to know him more. He tried to go down on me and take my underwear off. I quickly put my hand there to stop him. Both hands. He said “sorry” and then continued to perform oral on me with my underwear still on. He just pushed it to the side. I was confused and numb. I didn’t know what to do. I just let it happen thinking well maybe I want this? I had to keep rationing with myself because I thought if I stopped, he would get mad at me and make me leave. He performed oral a couple of times. Never once asking me if he could. He didn’t speak to me the entire time. Never asking if it was okay. Just doing what he wanted. I didn’t do much to him. I was just uncomfortable and confused by everything. At one point, he inserted his fingers in me. Actually, he forced them. It hurt so bad. The whole situation felt forced. No talking. No stopping. He wanted to get what he wanted out of it. After he was “done”, he got up and got ready. Barley talking to me. Basically rushed me out of his house to go hang with his cousins. It was like well, I got what I wanted so I’m done with you. I felt gross. The drive home, I cried the entire way. I felt used, disrespected and humiliated. But, at the same time I didn’t know why I was crying? I wanted this? Right? I went over there. I didn’t say no? But I didn’t say yes either. I also put my hands to stop and he ignored it. 

I didn’t talk to him that entire weekend. I kept ignoring him.  I didn’t understand why I didn’t want to talk to him? But something made me want nothing to do with him. I was in such denial. He asked me if I was mad at him after a couple of days  and I said that I didn’t think this was going to work. Sent this long text and said I felt used. He said that I was cool coming over there first. I told him I didn’t feel right about the situation. He said, “okay sorry.” And that was it. 

The few months after, I drank a lot. I would drink to numb it all out. It was getting to the point, I would drink to blackout. I would then have suicidal thoughts. The sad thing is, I would still try to talk  and reach out to him. I guess trying to make sense of it all? Or make it all seem okay. Thinking that it could help. I finally stopped after a while. I had this uneasy feeling and just wanted nothing to do with him. I was confused about my feelings towards him.

A couple of months later, I had a full blown mental breakdown. It was a lot of other things building up but that was the breaking point. I haven’t touched, kissed or dated anyone since him. I thought for so long something was wrong with me. I felt numb and closed off to all feelings towards sex and relationships. It took me two years and countless of other women’s stories to realize that what happened that night was not consensual. He never once asked me if it was okay, if I was okay, if this is what I wanted. He only cared about himself. He forced all of that on me. Taking my vulnerability and my care for him and using it for his own advantage. I’m still processing the hurt it caused me. Doubting myself and thinking I asked for it. Or it wasn’t a big deal. I will say, that situation, taught me the value of my self worth. I am going to therapy and working on the trauma it caused. I am working on realizing that it was not consensual. That how I acted was a way to survive and protect myself. That the numbness, confusion, guilt and denial are normal. I am working on realizing it wasn’t my fault. And how I deserved so much better. How there is a guy out there who will love and respect me. And not be a selfish asshole. And how consent in a relationship, is the most important things for BOTH people involved.
parent_comment: i went through the freezing thing also. i told myself that i wanted it since i didn’t fight him. i sadly feel for you on this one and i am so sorry that you went through smthng so terrible. i wish people understand the depth of their actions and how it affects us every single day until we learn to cope (if we do). thank you for sharing your story, i truly wish the best for you.

title: Trying to figure out if this instance was SA or not. It’s been on my mind.
body:
So I’m not sure what my orientation is, but I only date women and sometimes, when drunk, I hook up with men. I’m not sure if it’s because I actually want to, tbh. Sometimes I feel like it’s because my upbringing and old friends pressured me to be okay with it.

So about 5-6 years ago I started sleeping with men for the first time and there was this one guy I kinda regularly slept with. But i remember it being a chore to get him to get me off because straight up intercourse with dudes doesn’t do a damn thing for me. Eventually I just said that we should stop doing things all together and just be friends. 

The next time I came over to hang out, have a few drinks and game, he initiates stuff. I didn’t say no, I might add. It just kinda happened. When it was done, he said we should stop hooking up like that because I “never seem to want to play with [his] balls or anything” so that era of us hooking up was finally over. 

I’ve only recently got good at making sex stop when I don’t want it. I guess I’m asking on this one because, like I said, we had both been drinking and I didn’t exactly try to stop it.
parent_comment: If you didn’t want it to happen, it’s assault. The fact that you were drinking doesn’t matter. The fact that you didn’t actively protest doesn’t matter.   If you didn’t want it, it’s assault. I personally struggled with this for a long time since I thought that since I reluctantly said yes after all of his begging, I had consented. But consent obtained by begging, aggression, or assumption due to a partner’s silence on the matter is not consent at all. I’m so sorry this happened to you, stay safe as you continue to heal

title: I don't know if it counts as assault
body:

I have kissed them both in the past, just drunk innocent making out. The one friend I had done more with, but we hadn't had sex. 

At the end of the night I don't remember how I got back to the accommodation. One minute we were drinking in a garden then I was in my one friend's room and we were having sex.

I passed out in the middle of it. I woke up and he's still going. I didn't say anything. I just let him finish whatever he was doing. It was about 4 in the morning and I got up to leave. He walked me home.

I got up the next morning in serious pain. I was bleeding for the next two days. I haven't really spoke about it to anyone.

I mentioned it to a friend. I said that I fell asleep during sex and he carried on, didn't say who it was or how long ago it happened, just that I had experienced that in the past. My friend said it sounded 'rapeish' and I should talk to someone. I asked him not to talk to anyone about it, because I need to figure it out myself first. He accepted that and hasn't spoke if it since, which I'm grateful for.

I'm just confused. I don't think it's assault, I made a mistake and I regret it. But something in my head keeps saying that what happened wasn't right. He's my friend and he isn't the person to assault someone, let alone me. 

I don't know what I want to achieve by posting this here... if its validation that it was just a mistake I made after I drank to much. I can't talk to anyone in my life about it because I can't admit it to my family and I don't want to ask my friends in case it is and then they make me do something about it. 

I think I just need someone to tell me it was fine or not... then I can stop thinking about what happened and focus on moving on from it.

Thank you

Bean

title: Is this SA? And what do I do..

1. is the fear that people saw.
2. is the fear this might ruin her life.

ok. luckily, this will not ruin her life. At most there might be some School Discipline. There will be no crime or anything like that.

And you have already said that you don't think anyone saw. Trust yourself.
It was a very brief event, chances are no one was even looking in that direction. 
It was a mistake, not a spectacle. 

I think you should talk to her about it, I suspect you'll feel better about the situation after that chat, keep it light but firm. You don't have to accuse her of anything, but definitely make it clear how you feel. Set the boundary. 

You got this 💪

parent_comment: Being drunk in and of itself means that you are unable to give consent to sexual activity. I know plenty of people have “consensual” sex while drunk, I’ve done it myself, but legally it’s not because of things like this. Especially since you can’t remember what your response was when asked to try anal. The fact that you were so drunk that you were unable to communicate your fear and distress means that you were definitely too drunk to be having sex, and honestly there are some huge red flags that your ex orchestrated it on purpose (him not being as drunk as you, knowing that anal was a hard no, knowing that you were far too drunk to resist). The fact that you said to him multiple times that it hurt and asking for help is the real kicker here, because it doesn’t matter what happened up until that point, whether you were drunk or not, or whether you had consented. Consent to any sexual activity can be withdrawn AT ANY TIME. This was clearly you withdrawing your consent (or pseudo-consent in this situation) and wanting the activity to stop, of which he purposefully ignored you and the fact that you were clearly in pain did not stop him because “it felt really good” to him. This was a selfish act and completely violated your rights to your own body and your trust, and is without a doubt sexual abuse/assault. I know that you believe that he never meant to hurt you, I understand this mindset well, but I invite you to let go of this thought because if he truly didn’t mean to hurt or harm you in any way he would not have continued when he knew you were in pain. He was being selfish. And I’m so sorry that this happened to you. The fact that these memories are bothering you means that you should think about talking to some kind of professional about them, even if that just means texting or calling a SA hotline to ask their opinion. It can be very helpful to hear other people validating how you feel about these experiences. Just know that all of your emotions are valid x

title: I'm still stuck on everything that happened and it still affects my life
body:
I feel weird and disgusting 

English is not my first language, so sorry if there are any mistakes. Also, the text is quite long, so please forgive me in advance.

I don't know if this is considered rape per se, but I think it constitutes some level of abuse. My memories of it are very confusing; I know it happened, but there are memory lapses spanning years.

My family always gathers at my great-grandmother's house every Sunday. At the time, my aunt who lives with her was married to a man. He was always kind of strange, barely interacted with anyone, and usually stayed inside their bedroom. I can't remember exactly how it started, I just know he had a video game and invited me to play once. I was a child and, at the time, had never seen anything like it before, so I went. He started asking me to let him touch me. I was a child; I don't think I understood what that really meant. Then it got worse. He would ask me to lie down and he would start to suck on me, then he would ask me to suck him and touch him, among other things I'm not sure are worth mentioning. I clearly remember thinking after leaving my great-grandmother's house: "When I get home, I need to brush my teeth."

He never actually raped me (I don't know if that would be the correct way to say it), but it hurts. His touches hurt. It lasted a long time. He would take me to his room (sometimes I even went on my own, I don't know what was going through my head) and do what he wanted, and I hated going to my great-grandmother's house because of him. No one ever suspected (or if they did, they did nothing); I think they thought we were just "playing."

After a while, it became less frequent because I had started to understand it was wrong, so I avoided being alone with him.

It ended when I was about 10 (I'm 22 now) because he divorced my aunt. The last time I remember him touching me was when he hugged me from behind and squeezed my breast. I hate being trapped by this. I hate that he changed something in me, and that there's something strange in me because of him.

I know he has (or had, I haven't seen him in years) pictures of me because I remember him taking photos of my private parts. I'm afraid he still has them, afraid he might do something with them, that he's shown them to someone else. I don't know, so many things he could have done or not done with those damn pictures. I feel guilty that this happened. I know it's not my fault, that I was just a child, but there's a weight on me that says it is.

I don't know if it's true, but I suspect he did the same thing to his daughter. Maybe not, but there was an incident where she pointed a knife at him. Everyone thought she was crazy, but I knew what he was capable of. I knew and I said nothing. Talking about this is very painful for me, and it was only this year that I had the courage to tell someone, some friends of mine, but I don't think they understood me very well and downplayed it. I don't know.

I'm afraid I'm reliving this because I want to "get attention." I've always dealt with this, but in the last few months, it has been affecting me a lot because I keep remembering everything. This happens from time to time, when something related to abuse or something similar occurs in my life, like when a teacher three times my age asked me out alone. I felt bad at the time and I went back to the same trauma again, but that's another story.

My great-grandmother still lives in the same house where it all happened, so we still go there. Every time I pass by that room, I feel something bad. I remember the smell, the feeling of disgust. I just wish I could erase it.

Because of him, I think I learned about many things I shouldn't have known so early. My parents were always very liberal, never checked my phone, never worried about seeing if something was wrong with me, so I started consuming pornography very early. I would look at those things and remember myself, and a horrible feeling that I wanted it to happen again started to enter my head. I don't want to. But there's a strange desire in me that only feels pleasure if there's something at least somewhat forced involved. Is that normal? I masturbate thinking about him, thinking about everything that happened. I feel disgusting. I was just a child. Why?

Nowadays I feel somewhat apathetic. When I told one of my friends, he thought I was crazy because I was telling him while laughing. I didn't even realize I was laughing. I just can't cry in front of others when this is the topic. I only cry alone, in the middle of the night. Just because I feel dead about it doesn't mean it hurts less. Does that make sense?

I feel the consequences of this to this day. In my addiction to pornography and masturbation, in the way everyone in my family talks about him as if he's no big deal, in the scenarios I create in my head, in the stories I write where I torture my characters in a sick way. It seems like everything splatters back onto him and nothing is truly good.

My abuser is doing well today. And that scares me. I'm afraid he'll do it to other people (which he probably does), but I don't have the courage to actually report him. Will this haunt me forever?

Sometimes I want to invalidate my abuse, saying it wasn't that bad, that he didn't even really rape me, that other people suffer worse and don't keep going back to it, that they move on. Crazy, right? I was the victim and I feel guilty for not being able to move on, while he can.

Maybe this was confusing; it's just that my memories of it are too.

Thank you for reading this far. I needed to vent a little.
parent_comment:
I’m sorry this happened to you. The feelings and fantasies you are having are very common for sexual abuse victims. 

I experienced very similar things after I was violently raped. I thought I was going insane.  Like, why would I have such a strong desire to have it happen again??? I was not as young as you were. I was in my early 20s and still I had the same feelings. It got to the point I was actually putting myself in very dangerous situations with men I knew wouldn’t respect me or my boundaries.  

After a few years of this, I couldn’t live like that anymore and found a wonderful psychologist who specialized in helping sexual assault and abuse victims get themselves to a healthier and happier place. I don’t know your situation, but if it’s possible, I highly recommend talk therapy with a psychologist. They are there to help. And, you make the most progress when you find one you are comfortable enough to talk about your most delicate thoughts, feelings and reactions.  For me, my most shameful thing was that during this most violent assault, I orgasmed. That broke my brain. Like, how could I have such an intense orgasm during the worst thing that ever happened to me. My psychologist told me it’s normal and it was my body involuntarily reacting to stimuli, like a sneeze. Knowing that, helped me so much. 

There is a best selling book called, “The Body Keeps the Score” which helps you understand why your body seems to crave the trauma and offers proven methods to rewire your brain - the same methods top athletes use to improve their performance.  It’s on Amazon for about $11 USD.

A few things you need to know - 
- none of it was your fault, even the times you feel you initiated it. Children are very easily manipulated.
- It’s unfair to that little girl who went through all that to judge her with your adult brain. Her brain wasn’t developed enough to comprehend what was happening nor to have a defense. This is why there are laws protecting children.  Again, children are very easily manipulated.
- It’s not your job to keep his secret. Keeping this all to yourself (not telling anyone in your family or close circle) is causing you great mental anguish. If you need help talking with your family about this, a close friend actually had her psychologist invite them to her office and helped my friend tell her parents what happened in a safe place where her psychologist could help her parents with their reaction.  It worked out very well for her.
- What happened to you doesn’t define you or your future. 

I wish you strength and happiness. ❤️

title: I went in to get an ultrasound and I left with an IUD without my explicit consent
body:
Long story short, I went to the gynecologic with the intention of getting myself checked out and asking about birth control. I left with an IUD in tears.

Long story:

At the start of the visit (that was about 20 minutes) the doctor told me that the pills I wanted wouldn't be a great fit because of my weight. I said okay, in my mind thinking that then I wouldn't get anything. I had never been on hormones and I was a little scared of the possible mood swings and such. This was also my second ever trip to the gynecologist and I was really nervous.

She asked me if I had considered a contraceptive implant or an IUD, but I said that I was scared of them both because I wouldn't be able to get them out myself.

She just said that I should think it over and that she'd be able to put the IUD in right now. I said that I was scared of the pain, so if it would hurt a lot to put it in, then I don't want it. I said that I had read horror stories about it. She didn't really say anything to that, and we started the examination.

In the end, there was nothing wrong, and then I'm not completely sure what happened next because of the shock and the pain. Suddenly she's opening the box and inserting the IUD and I kind of blacked out, I know I was screaming and it was absolute hell. The worst pain of my life. I didn't even take a painkiller before because I didn't know it was going to happen.

The nurse that was by my head (I guess there to keep me calm) was also kind of chuckling and commenting that my eyes were really wide and telling me to breathe. I guess trauma is funny. They did keep asking me if I was okay, but I was in shock and just said yes, I guess.

So the doctor didn't really explain anything about the IUD (I know how it works since I've researched it but she didn't know that) and didn't really get my consent to put it in either. I didn't explicitly say no, but I think she should have made sure? She also kept asking me if I felt like she was pressuring me, and I think that it was sign that she felt like she WAS pressuring me.

So if we had paused at any point, I would have said no to the IUD, because I did not want one before the visit. But it was over kind of fast.

I left the office kind of in a haze, and then I broke down in tears at the bus stop. And now I'm traumatized and I don't want to go in again for my checkup in the summer. I'm thinking of filing a complaint.

Am I overreacting?

EDIT: Thank you all so much for the support and helping me to understand that this was much more serious than I first thought. It is much appreciated.

I have filed the complaint. I'll see how they respond and then I'll see if I'll take it further. I don't want to start a whole process, but I want the doctor to know she messed up.

Also, I checked the time of my bus ticket and the whole thing actually lasted closer to 30 minutes, which makes sense since there was the ultrasound as well. I guess that's a trauma response as well.

EDIT2: I did not sign anything. I don't know if you're supposed to do that here or not (I'm not in the US).

You can read in my story where I'm a little hazy because of the shock, but I am sure of that. I also never said yes to the IUD, I think she just assumed it was okay since I didn't say no either. She inserted it right after the the ultrasound. 

And it was not planned beforehand. Of that I'm sure we well, as I was just going to ask about birth control pills.

EDIT A MONTH LATER: I got an email from the senior physician of the department. It basically said "Sorry you felt like you were pressured. The doctor says you said yes to getting the IUD. There's nothing we can do about the pain anyway, bye." So it's basically my word against hers and I also had a problem with "You FELT like" so I responded, kindly. Just waiting on a response.
parent_comment: I'm pretty sure when I had mine in I had to sign some documents explaining I knew what was happening and that I was aware of side effects. This is just horrific, please do lodge a complaint. I hope you're OK OP.

title: I went in to get an ultrasound and I left with an IUD without my explicit consent
body:
Long story short, I went to the gynecologic with the intention of getting myself checked out and asking about birth control. I left with an IUD in tears.

Long story:

At the start of the visit (that was about 20 minutes) the doctor told me that the pills I wanted wouldn't be a great fit because of my weight. I said okay, in my mind thinking that then I wouldn't get anything. I had never been on hormones and I was a little scared of the possible mood swings and such. This was also my second ever trip to the gynecologist and I was really nervous.

She asked me if I had considered a contraceptive implant or an IUD, but I said that I was scared of them both because I wouldn't be able to get them out myself.

She just said that I should think it over and that she'd be able to put the IUD in right now. I said that I was scared of the pain, so if it would hurt a lot to put it in, then I don't want it. I said that I had read horror stories about it. She didn't really say anything to that, and we started the examination.

In the end, there was nothing wrong, and then I'm not completely sure what happened next because of the shock and the pain. Suddenly she's opening the box and inserting the IUD and I kind of blacked out, I know I was screaming and it was absolute hell. The worst pain of my life. I didn't even take a painkiller before because I didn't know it was going to happen.

The nurse that was by my head (I guess there to keep me calm) was also kind of chuckling and commenting that my eyes were really wide and telling me to breathe. I guess trauma is funny. They did keep asking me if I was okay, but I was in shock and just said yes, I guess.

So the doctor didn't really explain anything about the IUD (I know how it works since I've researched it but she didn't know that) and didn't really get my consent to put it in either. I didn't explicitly say no, but I think she should have made sure? She also kept asking me if I felt like she was pressuring me, and I think that it was sign that she felt like she WAS pressuring me.

So if we had paused at any point, I would have said no to the IUD, because I did not want one before the visit. But it was over kind of fast.

I left the office kind of in a haze, and then I broke down in tears at the bus stop. And now I'm traumatized and I don't want to go in again for my checkup in the summer. I'm thinking of filing a complaint.

Am I overreacting?

EDIT: Thank you all so much for the support and helping me to understand that this was much more serious than I first thought. It is much appreciated.

I have filed the complaint. I'll see how they respond and then I'll see if I'll take it further. I don't want to start a whole process, but I want the doctor to know she messed up.

Also, I checked the time of my bus ticket and the whole thing actually lasted closer to 30 minutes, which makes sense since there was the ultrasound as well. I guess that's a trauma response as well.

EDIT2: I did not sign anything. I don't know if you're supposed to do that here or not (I'm not in the US).

You can read in my story where I'm a little hazy because of the shock, but I am sure of that. I also never said yes to the IUD, I think she just assumed it was okay since I didn't say no either. She inserted it right after the the ultrasound. 

And it was not planned beforehand. Of that I'm sure we well, as I was just going to ask about birth control pills.

EDIT A MONTH LATER: I got an email from the senior physician of the department. It basically said "Sorry you felt like you were pressured. The doctor says you said yes to getting the IUD. There's nothing we can do about the pain anyway, bye." So it's basically my word against hers and I also had a problem with "You FELT like" so I responded, kindly. Just waiting on a response.
parent_comment: Ok wow. I used to work assisting an FNP who placed IUD’s. Every woman had a visit prior where she was educated about it and the risks/benefits.  If she came back with questions she got another visit to discuss. If she decided to proceed, she was scheduled during her menses as it made placement less painful. Prior to placement she was given two different consent forms to sign, one was the standard hospital consent for a procedure and one was IUD specific, laying out the risks (cramping, perforation, migration, etc.) and any last questions or concerns were asked about.  NO ONE got an IUD that they did not explicitly consent to. Also, there are at least 4 different types of IUDs that we placed, and each women was counseled on the risks/benefits of each type and why or why not each was a good option for her. I’m so sorry about what happened to you. It’s not remotely ok. Please please please speak to anyone and everyone you can about this. Get ahold of their procedure policy, I’m horrified by what they did to you and am really concerned that this is standard practice for them.

title: Was it rape?

Despite how kind he was, he did have a bad habit of pressuring me often into things I wasn’t quite comfortable with. For example, I had my first kiss with him about 3 months after we began dating, which was a direct effect of him asking over and over again over a span of weeks. However, I realize that he should’ve never gone through with it, since he literally had to cover my eyes because I was so terrified and frozen. The pressuring and guilting continued for months regarding more significant actions, which I always eventually caved in. The biggest problem was him continuing to ask me on a frequent basis, and then acting completely defeated after I would say no. He would often complain about not feeling “satisfied” in our relationship because of these refusals, which I would take on completely through guilt. However, one thing that I refused to cave on was sex. It was already a taboo topic for me, but I was 15 and didn’t feel ready for it. I had expressed for months that it wasn’t something I would even be willing to consider until I was 18. I have found journals from that time, though, that was trying to plead when he would speak of unhappiness and the possibility of breaking up because of it, saying “I’ve though about trying to comply so that he is happy”. Despite this, I am positive my boundaries were very clear. In May of the following year, he ended up breaking up with me because I refused to have sex with him. He soon returned and said it was the worst mistake he made, although it was still something he would continue to ask about. Then, two weeks later on my 16th birthday, we were in my room, and he was pressing me again. I really felt responsible for his happiness, so, stupidly, I consented to him rubbing down on the vulva, although stated that I wasn’t consenting to sex. Suddenly, as I was pressed against the bed frame, I felt him begin to push inside, which sent a surge of panic through me. I quickly began repeating “no no no” in a distressed manner, and I felt him continue to push inside. What I do remember, though, is that he never pushed all the way in, which makes me question the validity of the occasion. I regained control of my body and pushed him off of me. I began sobbing and curled up in a ball, and he came over immediately to apologize and ask if I was okay. I guess I didn’t really question the occasion and shrugged it off as miscommunication, although it always bugged me in the back of my head. After that, I took on sex as my responsibility in our relationship, as he would typically complain about it being too long since we had engaged in that. That being said, it would often be about 4-5 times a week. He often guilted me into it, and I felt as though I became somebody only useful for sex. Fast forward to January of the next year, and my dad found out about the whole situation. This acted as a catalyst for me to begin questioning the circumstances of the situation, and open it up to the possibility of sexual assault. I confronted him about it, and he at first told me that he didn’t realize he was inside and that he didn’t remember me saying no. However, I didn’t feel as though the “no” was relevant because I very clearly never gave him consent and was obviously distressed. Also, I had made it clear for months that I wouldn’t consent to this. It felt very frustrated because I didn’t want to chalk up something that felt very violating to just a miscommunication or “gray area”. After about 2 hours of talking, he finally admitted that in the moment he was just eager to get the opportunity, was prioritizing and focusing on himself and his own wants, and was ignoring me and what I was saying. I feel like I let it get to that point by consenting to lesser things. I should’ve fought back more physically or yelled no louder. Maybe I just want to be a victim. He’s a good person and cared about me, and I don’t think it was out of malicious intent. I didn’t give me that respect, nor did he give me respect in the months previous with other boundaries. The other previous actions I did ultimately consent to, so I don’t have anyone else to blame but me. I was just coerced and manipulated, but I said yes. Sex, I never said yes to. What happened was I was at his house. I was hanging out with him on his couch, he made a lot of sexual comments and jokes toward me. parent_comment:
I am a prosecutor who handles sex cases.  Depending upon the state you live in, your age alone might make the event criminal.  Statutory rape is based on the age of the victim; consent is not relevant because the law does not allow minors to consent to such acts.  As for the crime of rape where the issue of consent is central to the crime, the actions you described could suggest that you did consent.  By saying “could suggest” doesn’t mean I am saying you did consent, instead I am pointing out that others could see this as a consensual encounter, meaning there is doubt as to whether he engaged in unconsensual sex.  He will likely claim that you agreed to have sex; the fact you said “no” multiple times before eventually saying yes would be irrelevant in the eyes of some jurors absent evidence of duress on his part - such as threats if you didn’t change your mind.  Preying upon your psychological desires to please and not disappoint is very sick, but it likely would not rise to the level of duress. 

Because criminal cases must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt, cases where doubt exists should not be filed.  As a prosecutor I can say this is a case my office would likely not file as a rape case - given your age however we would likely file a statutory rape case.  I do encourage you to file a police report.  More importantly, please seek some professional counseling - you have clearly been victimized and professionals can help you process all of this.  Also, professionals can help you learn to establish boundaries with intimate partners so that you can have healthy and happy relationships in the future.  My best to you.

I do encourage you to file a police report.  More importantly, please seek some professional counseling - you have clearly been victimized and professionals can help you process all of this. It is reassuring to hear the change you have seen in him. It sounds sincere based on your description, and I truly hope it is.

It is a tragic situation when two people love each other and something gets broken that can't be repaired. Unfortunately it does happen. I honestly think your best outlet will probably be to speak with a professional, if possible. I know it can be difficult to arrange. With anyone else you will have your hands full dealing with their reaction to your situation, which will leave very little room for dealing with your own reaction.

It sounds like the challenge in discussing it with him is finding a way to do it productively. What are you looking to get from discussing it with him? One angle that might help is saying exactly what you said here, namely that his reaction since that event has been really helpful in restoring your trust. That you are having a difficult time separating out your feeling about this event from your overall state of mental health caused by the stress of the past year, as well as other situations you say you are repressing your reaction to. It's possible you would be still struggling even if that trauma had never occurred. There is no way to know for sure, but if you have suffered other traumas in your life then it is entirely possible. What could he do that would make you feel supported? If you have some specific and actionable ask from him, it will probably feel a lot more productive. If you need to vent, it will probably just shut him down. That's my best guess.

It also might help to tackle your overall mental health intentionally. Make space in your life for the things you enjoy. Give yourself something to look forward to. Make a good memory when you have a chance, to sustain you through the week. Do you think that might help?

title: I went in to get an ultrasound and I left with an IUD without my explicit consent
body:
Long story short, I went to the gynecologic with the intention of getting myself checked out and asking about birth control. I left with an IUD in tears.

Long story:

At the start of the visit (that was about 20 minutes) the doctor told me that the pills I wanted wouldn't be a great fit because of my weight. I said okay, in my mind thinking that then I wouldn't get anything. I had never been on hormones and I was a little scared of the possible mood swings and such. This was also my second ever trip to the gynecologist and I was really nervous.

She asked me if I had considered a contraceptive implant or an IUD, but I said that I was scared of them both because I wouldn't be able to get them out myself.

She just said that I should think it over and that she'd be able to put the IUD in right now. I said that I was scared of the pain, so if it would hurt a lot to put it in, then I don't want it. I said that I had read horror stories about it. She didn't really say anything to that, and we started the examination.

In the end, there was nothing wrong, and then I'm not completely sure what happened next because of the shock and the pain. Suddenly she's opening the box and inserting the IUD and I kind of blacked out, I know I was screaming and it was absolute hell. The worst pain of my life. I didn't even take a painkiller before because I didn't know it was going to happen.

The nurse that was by my head (I guess there to keep me calm) was also kind of chuckling and commenting that my eyes were really wide and telling me to breathe. I guess trauma is funny. They did keep asking me if I was okay, but I was in shock and just said yes, I guess.

So the doctor didn't really explain anything about the IUD (I know how it works since I've researched it but she didn't know that) and didn't really get my consent to put it in either. I didn't explicitly say no, but I think she should have made sure? She also kept asking me if I felt like she was pressuring me, and I think that it was sign that she felt like she WAS pressuring me.

So if we had paused at any point, I would have said no to the IUD, because I did not want one before the visit. But it was over kind of fast.

I left the office kind of in a haze, and then I broke down in tears at the bus stop. And now I'm traumatized and I don't want to go in again for my checkup in the summer. I'm thinking of filing a complaint.

Am I overreacting?

EDIT: Thank you all so much for the support and helping me to understand that this was much more serious than I first thought. It is much appreciated.

I have filed the complaint. I'll see how they respond and then I'll see if I'll take it further. I don't want to start a whole process, but I want the doctor to know she messed up.

Also, I checked the time of my bus ticket and the whole thing actually lasted closer to 30 minutes, which makes sense since there was the ultrasound as well. I guess that's a trauma response as well.

EDIT2: I did not sign anything. I don't know if you're supposed to do that here or not (I'm not in the US).

You can read in my story where I'm a little hazy because of the shock, but I am sure of that. I also never said yes to the IUD, I think she just assumed it was okay since I didn't say no either. She inserted it right after the the ultrasound. 

And it was not planned beforehand. Of that I'm sure we well, as I was just going to ask about birth control pills.

EDIT A MONTH LATER: I got an email from the senior physician of the department. It basically said "Sorry you felt like you were pressured. The doctor says you said yes to getting the IUD. There's nothing we can do about the pain anyway, bye." So it's basically my word against hers and I also had a problem with "You FELT like" so I responded, kindly. Just waiting on a response.

We talked briefly, and I asked him what he was looking for. He said something along the lines of a kinky sex partner and someone to hang out with. He identified as a dom. We texted, and had a brief conversation about what we were into. I'll leave out all the details, but he asked me how I feel about anal sex and swallowing cum. I told him I was curious about both, not that I was down to try them. That was all I said: I was curious. The conversation, again, was brief, and we didn't get into much or establish any boundaries.

I messaged him to hang out after attending a funeral. I was in a really fucked up place, super depressed and lonely. Not that that's an excuse, but it does give some insight into my mindset at the time. Sex was a negative coping mechanism for me for a long time. So I went over to his place.

Things went right to sex. And if this genuinely isn't SA, please feel free to tell me, I can take it.

I didn’t feel confident in the relationship. He started becoming more distant and I kept holding on. Thinking maybe it could work. But I still had that feeling that something was off. That this isn’t what a relationship should be. I was too insecure at the time to trust myself. 

We were suppose to hang out the day after thanksgiving. An hour before, he tried to bail. He wanted to go hang with his cousins. I was crushed. Then, he said I could come over to hang out before he left. Deep down, I knew better but I still went over. He was leaving crumbs and I was taking them. When I got over, none of his roommates where there so I thought we would hang out in the living room. Nope. He took me straight upstairs to his room. We were laying on his bed and I was trying to make small talk. I thought we could watch a movie. He wasn’t saying much. But just enough to keep me there. I felt uncomfortable but thought I was overreacting. He started making out with me. Not romantic at all like he was getting what was “his”. It felt kind of forced. I went along with it. I loved to makeout and it wasn’t unusual but I felt that this time it was different. Clothes started to come off. But, I didn’t want to do more than that. He said “sorry” and then continued to perform oral on me with my underwear still on. He just pushed it to the side. I was confused and numb. I didn’t know what to do. I just let it happen thinking well maybe I want this? I had to keep rationing with myself because I thought if I stopped, he would get mad at me and make me leave. He performed oral a couple of times. Never once asking me if he could. He didn’t speak to me the entire time. Never asking if it was okay. Just doing what he wanted. I didn’t do much to him. I was just uncomfortable and confused by everything. At one point, he inserted his fingers in me. Actually, he forced them. It hurt so bad. The whole situation felt forced. No talking. No stopping. He wanted to get what he wanted out of it. After he was “done”, he got up and got ready. Barley talking to me. Basically rushed me out of his house to go hang with his cousins. It was like well, I got what I wanted so I’m done with you. I felt gross. The drive home, I cried the entire way. I felt used, disrespected and humiliated. But, at the same time I didn’t know why I was crying? I wanted this? Right? I went over there. I didn’t say no? But I didn’t say yes either. I also put my hands to stop and he ignored it. 

I didn’t talk to him that entire weekend. I kept ignoring him.  I didn’t understand why I didn’t want to talk to him? But something made me want nothing to do with him. I was in such denial. He asked me if I was mad at him after a couple of days  and I said that I didn’t think this was going to work. Sent this long text and said I felt used. He said that I was cool coming over there first. I told him I didn’t feel right about the situation. He said, “okay sorry.” And that was it. 

The few months after, I drank a lot. I would drink to numb it all out. It was getting to the point, I would drink to blackout. I would then have suicidal thoughts. The sad thing is, I would still try to talk  and reach out to him. I guess trying to make sense of it all? Or make it all seem okay. Thinking that it could help. I finally stopped after a while. I had this uneasy feeling and just wanted nothing to do with him. I was confused about my feelings towards him.

A couple of months later, I had a full blown mental breakdown. It was a lot of other things building up but that was the breaking point. I haven’t touched, kissed or dated anyone since him. I thought for so long something was wrong with me. I felt numb and closed off to all feelings towards sex and relationships. It took me two years and countless of other women’s stories to realize that what happened that night was not consensual. He never once asked me if it was okay, if I was okay, if this is what I wanted. He only cared about himself. He forced all of that on me. Taking my vulnerability and my care for him and using it for his own advantage. I’m still processing the hurt it caused me. Doubting myself and thinking I asked for it. Or it wasn’t a big deal. I will say, that situation, taught me the value of my self worth. I am going to therapy and working on the trauma it caused. I am working on realizing that it was not consensual. That how I acted was a way to survive and protect myself. That the numbness, confusion, guilt and denial are normal. I am working on realizing it wasn’t my fault. And how I deserved so much better. How there is a guy out there who will love and respect me. And not be a selfish asshole. And how consent in a relationship, is the most important things for BOTH people involved.

title: I was a child witness of sexual assult. How do I move on as an adult?
body:
When I turned 7, my elder brother became a legal adult, at 18. When he was in his early twenties, we had a teenage cousin (and her family) move into our home. Over time, my brother and my teenage cousin started having a secret, sexual relationship.

I saw them a few times in the act: her sitting his lap, dirty dancing,  touching (in private or in public). They would do this in front of me with no boundaries. I was forced to keep it a secret. Even when the adults figured it out, they told me the same. (I found out their relationship was sexual when I overheard the adults talking to them about what to do if my cousin got pregnant.)

I intuitively felt it was wrong at that age but had no authority to do/say anything. I was burdened with this knowledge and I started getting in trouble at school at that age and I never knew why I was acting up or zoning out. (Started sleep-walking and had major, unaddressed stress/anxiety.) I felt helpless that I couldn’t do or say anything and I assumed both my cousin and brother were old enough to know what they were doing. And at that age, everyone was an adult.

Now that I am an adult, I realize my cousin was only 15 at the time. She was a child. And I’ve long since gone no-contact with my brother which he is angry about but I don’t think he knows I did this because of this “family secret.” No one ever talks about it. TBH, I don’t talk to my cousin either. We drifted apart right after her family moved out of our home. I assume they moved out because of this fiasco.

I’m angry, and confused and I want to know if this is considered sexual assault on my end, having been a child and a witness. Or would it have another name? It’s plagued me and my thoughts for a long time and sometimes affects how intimate I feel in my current relationships. i.e., it crosses my mind and I completely shut down intimately and don’t want to go any further. 

I don't know how to find closure from this past trauma. I've been advised to take journaling more seriously but I feel guilt over not doing something or speaking up. I wonder if volunteer work for SA and DV survivors would be a more proactive solution.
parent_comment: While assault requires physical touch, what you experienced is still absolutely sexual abuse. I’m so sorry you had to witness that.

parent_comment:
>Later when confronted they said that they only heard me say I wasn't sure and one no.

That is two clear instances of you setting boundaries. It sounds like your partner is holding onto some pretty toxic ideas around consent. This doesn't mean your partner is a bad person- society conditions people to think a "no" or "I'm not sure" means "convince me." It takes a lot of conscious work to undo that conditioning and replace it with healthy communication and the respect of boundaries.

From your perspective as a SA survivor, I imagine it seems like you have been incredibly clear, which makes the violation feel so much worse. Those feelings are completely valid. However, what seems clear and obvious to you as a survivor might seem completely alien and confusing to your partner, because they don't have the same frame of reference and have a hard time empathizing or understanding.

There are some really great beginner resources out there about how to communicate with someone who has experienced SA, as well as the basics of how consent works and how to set and respect boundaries. I will link some of my favourites below.

When you are in a long term relationship with someone (even if that relationship is not romantic or sexual), you make a commitment to do the hard work necessary to make sure the other person feels safe, comfortable, and happy with you. Your partner has made this commitment to you, and while it will not be an easy process for either of you, you both owe it to yourselves and your future relationships (again, including friendships) to work on these skills and build something stronger together.

If couples counseling is an option, I highly recommend it. If not, therapy for yourself might help you to identify the root of what you're feeling, as well as skills and resources to help talk about it in ways that are constructive. There are also plenty of good free resources on moving on from assault if cost is a barrier.

Good resources:

VIDEO: Empathy vs Sympathy (how to help and not help someone who has disclosed something painful): https://youtu.be/KZBTYViDPlQ

ARTICLE: Helping a Survivor of Sexual Assault https://www.wm.edu/offices/wellness/counselingcenter/students/sexualassault/index.php

WEBSITE: Consent, Communication, and Confidence Toolkits (very accessible way to learn the basics of consent, how to communicate boundaries, and being confident in sexual situations, with concrete examples and explanations) https://rasara.org/consent-toolkit

ARTICLE: Tips for Talking with Survivors of Sexual Assault https://www.rainn.org/articles/tips-talking-survivors-sexual-assault

BOOK: The Body Keeps the Score (AMAZING read about how trauma works- a phenomenal resource to help you realize your reactions and feelings are normal, and ways that people have been able to move forward) https://www.amazon.ca/dp/0143127748/ref=cm_sw_r_apan_glt_i_FYC1X6B2FG8RJH8CJ3FK?_encoding=UTF8&psc=1

What your partner did was not okay, and you have every right to feel upset and violated. I truly hope that the two of you are able to learn and grow from this experience to build a stronger and healthier relationship. ❤️

It's totally normal to be overwhelmed, and there's no standard timeline for where you need to be and when. Only share what you're ready to at any given moment. If a therapist asks you a question you aren't ready to answer, or if you get to a point and can't say any more, "I'm not ready to get into that" is an acceptable answer. Pressuring yourself too much can have several different unintended consequences. Every step, no matter how small or insignificant it feels, is progress to be proud of. Try to give yourself some grace.

You can "pressure" yourself in a healthy way. There's a difference between wanting/needing to process something specific but having anxiety over it and not being ready to process it. For me, I can usually tell the difference by talking around it, usually to myself at first. If talking around something without going into detail helps me give more detail, then I figure I probably am ready. If I talk around it and just freak out more, I'm probably not. You might have another method that works better, but I think finding a way to differentiate is really helpful.

Good luck, especially with finding a therapist you click with. If you have a few sessions and you don't like them, you can look for someone else. We don't always find the right one the first time, and it isn't always the therapist's fault. Sometimes you just don't have the kind of connection you need for it to work well, and they tend to be really understanding of that.

I have a pretty high alcohol tolerance, and remember being pretty sober (moreso tipsy but definitely not drunk or even blackout.) This is where it gets messy. I am very happy in my relationship, he is a wonderful person and my best friend. From what very little I remember, the sex hurt and it seemed quite aggressive. Everything in me tells me I would not have consented to this. I would never ever put my boyfriend in that position. We live together and he was expecting me to come back to our flat at 1am.

My next memory is me walking through random fields and forests with no clue where I am. Literally in the middle of the countryside. My phone is dead and I am so disorientated and confused that I genuinely thought I was near my hometown that is two and a half hours away from where I live currently at University. It turned out I was over a half an hour drive from my flat. I must have been walking for hours and then suddenly I see two older men who let me use their phone to call my mum, who then called my boyfriend who drove to me to pick me up. This is at around 10/11am, I had work at 8am that day and had every intention of going. My boyfriend immediately knew something was wrong, he went to the police when I didn’t come home, and even went to my work at the University to see if I had showed up or called in sick. He was so worried about me, and immediately sensed that I may have been raped. The truth is that I couldn’t remember anything, I had completely blacked out and had no recollection of a name or even a face, no idea where I was and no clue whether I was possible of consenting to this in the state I was in. As soon as I get home, I am throwing up for hours. I was so sick that my boyfriend was about to take me the hospital. This felt worse than any hangover I’ve ever had, and considering I didn’t drink enough that would ordinarily get me into the state I was in, I was concerned I was spiked. I couldn’t even stand up and was throwing up non stop for hours on end and was so confused about what had happened.

Police came to my flat to check that I was okay. I explained to them that I had no memory of how I got to where I was, and that my phone was dead. I explained how according to bank transactions, I ended up at another bar alone (again assuming, I have no memory of meeting this guy so very well could have been with him) on the way back home to my flat (again, something I would never do and I have no memory of). I said how I used another persons phone to call my boyfriend. They asked if I had any pelvic pain, insinuating possible sexual assault, but I genuinely was so ill that I could barely be present in conversation, and felt uncomfortable telling the truth in front of these two male police officers. I said that I didn’t. The truth is I did. I was just terrified that I may have actually consented in my altered state. 

I have an IUD, and have already booked for an STD test. It has been well under a day since this happened, about 12 hours since I got back to my flat and maybe 17 hours since I had sex (an estimate.) I feel so guilty, my boyfriend has been so supportive and yet I am so ashamed to tell him the truth- that I had sex with this man and barely remember a thing. It would shatter his world, but I know he deserves the truth. I am still trying to gather my thoughts to say it in the right way.

I was shocked to find out that I had a follower request from the guy who slept with me. At first, I ignored it, but then I briefly accepted to try and figure out what he knew, and whether he was drunk or not. From what he said- he knew that I had a boyfriend because I had told him, and he found it funny. He was drinking, but from what I can tell he was much more sober than me. I would NEVER do that sober. Was I spiked? Do I report it, now having a name of the guy? How do I tell my boyfriend. Hello love,

I am so so deeply sorry that this happened to you and that you are going through this. Of course you are deeply hurt, confused, ashamed and even feel guilt. First, I want to say that that is all so normal given what you have gone through. More importantly, I want to be very clear that this is NOT your fault. 

You know yourself. Everything you have just shared with us makes it very clear that you did not consent to this. You are happy in your relationship with no interest of sleeping with anyone outside of it. You usually handle your liquor well. You were pretty sober— maybe tipsy, but definitely not blackout to the point where you barely remember the night, how you wound up in bed with  a stranger or found yourself in a field almost two hours from home the next morning and missed work. None of that is normal or okay. I know you are spiraling and questioning everything, but I want to ask you to please do your best to quiet your mind and trust your gut right now. Trust yourself. 

I also want to say that even IF you had “consented” in that state— that is not consent. If you are not sober enough to make a sound decision about having sex with someone, especially someone you do not know, that is not informed consent. That man knew better. He also knew you were in a relationship. He knew you were in no state to have sex— even if he hadn’t spiked your drink. But it is very clear that he spiked your drink and took advantage of you. That is assault.

It also makes sense that you felt scared and uncomfortable to report what happened to the police— especially two men. That is so common, especially when you feel confused and ashamed on top of it all. It’s okay. You did what you felt comfortable with and that is the best you can do, okay? Don’t punish yourself for doing your best in a very scary and painful situation, please. You don’t deserve that. 

I imagine if you don’t tell your boyfriend, it will eat at you and you will feel guilty for something you did not do. For that reason, I would tell him if or when you feel ready to relieve yourself of that weight. My hope is that he is supportive, because that is what you need right now and sharing what happened to you with someone you love and trust can be healing after an experience like this. If you do not think he will handle it well and it will only bring you more pain and stress, then don’t tell him. Do what is *best for you* right now. Only tell him if and when you feel ready. If you don’t tell him, is there someone else you can talk to? Or maybe you could share with someone else *first* and then eventually share with him? Is there an older adult you can share with, maybe another woman?

He may feel upset about what happened, but I would hope that those feelings are upset for what happened to you and not that someone had sex with you while blacked out. You did not do anything wrong. You are young, so I don’t know how he will react or if he is mature enough to understand these things, but I hope he is and does. Regardless of how he reacts, I want to reiterate again and again that *none of this is your fault.*

The fact that this man reached out to you afterwards is fucking disgusting. The audacity. My last note is that since you now know his identity, I might report him while everything is fresh, but only if you feel comfortable. I might also go to a hospital and speak with a woman specifically to ask for an evidence kit, so that you have proof. Again, only do this if you feel comfortable. Please don’t put yourself through anything that feels too overwhelming right now. I am only making a suggestion as an outsider looking out for your wellbeing in the case that you do want to press charges in the future.  

Thank you for having the courage to share this with us, especially when everything is so fresh and overwhelming. I am sending you so much love and care while you go through this. Please do your best to take care of yourself and know that you are not alone.

title: Something weird happened with a friend from school and I don't know how to feel about it
body:

I was terrified for my first day, but then I met this guy (18) and we quickly made friends. We didn't go out or stuff like that, he just introduced me to his group and we kept being friendly while on school grounds. Then we began to chat online and he asked to see me. I said yes cause why not.

He insisted that we go to his place, but I didn't want to. Not because I was afraid of him, but because I am not a sociable person and I enjoy my time alone and I just wished to be home. I said yes cause he was relentless and we took a cab back to his place (he doesn't live with his family, they had a falling out). Once there things were really sweet and we cuddled and kissed, things I was confortable with, but then it just took a turn.

I wanted to go home, he insisted I stay for a bit and began touching me. I didn't say no cause I enjoyed it (just second base) and when he tried to go to third I told him no. He kept begging, I kept saying no, he asked for a reason and I said that the fact that I don't want to is reason enough. For a second I was really afraid he wouldn't care that I said no.

He got mad, sat back on the bed and didn't talk to me anymore. I don't even know why I tried to make peace with him and please him (I only do this with people I'm afraid of losing, yes a toxic trait, and I am not afraid of losing him). I kept trying to talk to him, he kept saying that is his way of showing its legit and I said that I'm not the type of person to go head first (I'm demisexual, which means I feel sexual attraction only after connecting mentally. I don't mind kissing and basic petting, but anything beyond that it's a nono until I feel connected)

He said that if I'll stay a little bit longer he won't get mad, so I did. Then he kept saying how he wished he could touch me, that it'll torment him that he couldn't, he doesn't even want sex, just to please me and I finally said okay. Felt uncomfortable, but he got to third base and I was just not enjoying it at all, feeling like crying. I told him to stop and he did.

Asked if anything was wrong, I told him no, but I just felt like crying. I just wanted to go home and cry my eyes out. This will sound disgusting but I feel like my private parts are on fire and I just don't know how to describe the feeling in my soul.

I don't want to say he SAed me because it doesn't feel like it. He stopped when I said it, but I just can't help but feel so sad and hollow. I don't know how to go on, how to act around him and what to do next. Of course I won't tell anyone since it wasn't like he raped me, he did stop, but I just want some advice on what to do and if I should keep in contact with him and forget this, I don't even know if he thinks we're in a relationship honestly. What should I do if he does think that? How do I let him down without ruining our friendship? Is this even sexual assault?

PS: I wanted to put the flair advice too, but it wouldn't let me choose to flairs, I hope it isn't bad I asked for advice.

Thank you all for reading this full on essay.
parent_comment:
This was 100% sexual assault.

If there was penetration of any kind(penis, fingers, toys etc.) It also classifies as rape.

What you experienced was sexual assault by coercion.

Sexual coercion is unwanted sexual activity that happens after being _pressured_ in nonphysical ways that include:

1. _Being worn down by someone who repeatedly asks for sex._

2. Being lied to or being promised things that weren’t true to trick you into having sex.

3. Having someone threaten to end a relationship, spread rumors about you or _display that you will be treated badly_ if you don’t have sex with them.   

4. Having an authority figure use their influence or authority to pressure you into having sex.

In a healthy relationship, you never have to have sexual contact when you don’t want to.

Sexual contact without your consent is assault.  

If someone fails to get consent the first time and has to continue pressuring the person to finally get consent?  That is not enthusiastic consent, it's not real consent and that person does not care whether the other party wanted the sexual contact.

When a person pressures you for consent they are not actually asking for consent, they are making sure you are going to take the responsibility for what _they're_ about to do to you.

You didn't want what happened, you made it clear and in a way you even asked him to drop it by explaining your sexuality and he continued to whine, complain, guilt trip and pressure you into doing what he wanted.

When a person actually cares about your pleasure they will absolutely care about your consent.  

I suggest not interacting with this person again in any way if possible and pressing charges if you're comfortable with that.

I'm not going to lie to you: reporting sexual assaults especially like these are very hard on the victim and can even backfire and you may end up getting sued if the attacker is rich or powerful enough/has rich or powerful friends.

The main reason most victims decide to report is because assailants _almost always try again_, if not with you than with someone else.

_  
Some examples of sexual coercion:  
 
**Wearing you down by asking for sex again and again or making you feel bad, _guilty, or obligated._**   
•“If you really loved me, you’d do it.”
•“Come on; it’s my birthday.”
•_“You don’t know what you do to me.”_

**Making you feel like it’s too late to say no.**   
•_“But you’ve already gotten me all worked up.”_
•“You can’t just make someone stop in the middle.”

**Telling you that not having sex will hurt your relationship.**   
•“Everything’s perfect. Why do you have to ruin it?”

There are more.

parent_comment:
I think that part of the problem is that you've internalized guilt about every possible decision you could make. You feel guilty if you consider saying no, but you were also taught to feel guilty if you say yes by your ex who made you feel like what you could give wasn't good enough, and you feel guilty if you don't communicate clearly and precisely, and you feel guilty for even feeling your feelings.

In reality, you have nothing to feel guilty about, because you haven't done literally anything wrong. It's not bad to have complicated feelings. It's not bad to have trouble speaking up in an uncomfortable situation. It doesn't make *you* bad to have had a bad sexual experience. You don't have to suddenly decide that you're magically okay and sex means nothing and your comfort isn't important, but I think you need to learn not to come down on yourself like this. It may help to talk to somebody professional.

And it's up to you if you want to see that guy again or not. If it's going to hurt you emotionally, you don't have to. If you are sure he wasn't trying to be predatory, you could try talking to him and see how he responds, or you don't have to. But I don't think anything good will come from continuing to put other people's feelings/comfort ahead of your own. Whether he intended to or not, he *did* do something wrong--he was careless and insensitive to you at best.

Hey bud, this was definitely assault.

Follow-up to your freezing and going with what he wanted stuff is that when in danger, our brains have more than just the fight or flight mode - it's fight, flight, freeze, and fawn. Everyone knows fight or flight, but not necessarily freeze or fawn.

The fawn response is when our brains see the danger again and the primal, survival parts of the brain thinks that the best way out is to go along with whatever our attacker wants, no matter how much it sucks - ergo, you going along with it the second time that day. Again, it's not your fault.

There's more reasons for staying in an abusive relationship, but that's not really my area of expertise. I'd like to reiterate that none of it is your fault At All, and I hope you have an affordable therapy option so that you can work through this with a professional's help.

title: I cant tell if it was SA or a False Memory?
body:

Starting from around the age of 12 or 13, I've had this vivid dream of my dad molesting me. I can see every single detail crystal clear in my head - the light coming from the TV and doorway, what channel it was on, what covers I had on my bed. In the dream/memory, I'm woken up to my dad in a t-shirt and boxers pulling my underwear up from my ankles, pulling the covers up over my body, kissing my forehead, and telling me to go back to sleep. In the dream or memory, I'm around the age of 6 - 8 years old. I vividly remember him being drunk in this memory as well.

I've never been uncomfortable around my dad in the slightest which is always conflicting when I have this dream/memory- I feel like I would be more uncomfortable around him if something like this actually happened but I don't know. After the age of 6 or 7- the age I was in this situation, I started getting very uncomfortable with my own body and being touched without initiating it and still am.
