I am also, to this day, completely unenthused and even disgusted at the thought of engaging sexually with another person. It makes me extremely anxious- and that's not to say I don't have a sex drive or experience attraction- but any time I've even gotten close to participating with someone else I've gotten so sick I've almost (and have on one occasion) thrown up. I hate it, I hate everything about it. 

I still find it odd, though. I'm completely comfortable around my father. I was a "daddy's girl," and he treats me like im his absolute pride and joy. I've been assaulted before (in which I know it has actually happened and I have not created some sort of false childhood memory) and the thought of being in the same room as one of those men makes me angry and sad- yet I have none of these feelings associated with my dad. However, it's entirely possible it *did* happen. 

My dad has been a chronic alcoholic my entire life and was sexually abused himself by his own father - as far as I know, at least. He doesn't talk about it, but I've pieced things together from stuff he told my mom before their divorce. He goes on benders and doesn't remember anything the day after - and it's a true, full blackout. I can tell when he's lying about not remembering and when he actually can't. He also has a history of womanizing and has allegedly sexually assaulted some if not most of his female co-workers and employees when he was younger. He's even been creepy to some of my friends- no touching or anything - but pointed sexual comments about them. My mom has also stated that the night I was conceived, he had gotten my mom drunk, and knowing she was getting ready to leave him, baby trapped her with me. He was also verbally abusive to my older brothers. All this to say basically, my dad is not and has never been a good person, especially when it comes to young women. 

It's hard, though. I love him. He's my dad. Other than this one specific memory, he has never touched me inappropriately, and other than a few drunken comments about me looking just like my mother, he has never even suggested the notion of doing anything inappropriate. And even though I know he's a bad person who has done objectively awful things to people I love, I can't hate him. He's always been there for me. He's my number one supporter. He was there for every softball game, every concert, play, and daddy-daughter dance. He still calls me Kiddo even though I'm 20 and in college. 

I don't know anymore. I'm almost disgusted with myself for even thinking he could do that to me. To a child. But it's just so clear in my head. I had the dream for the first time in a while, and I just can't stop thinking about it. It makes me sick and sad. Obviously, though, I can't just up and ask him about it. Either A) it did happen and our relationship is changed and forever ruined or B) I've somehow created a false memory, pretty much accused him of sexually assaulting me as a child, and our relationship is changed and forever ruined. I'm stuck between a rock and a hard place, and I'm tearing myself apart because *I don't even know if it really happened.*

I showed a lot of signs of being assaulted as a kid - the behavior change I mentioned previously - I also started bed wetting again for about a 6 month long period around the aforementioned time, etc. I also started self harming at a very young age as well for no real discernable reason. I feel like there's just too much supporting evidence for it to be a false memory, but somehow, I'm more terrified that it's false than if it's real. Like, somehow, my brain just decided to create something so disgustingly horrific and pin it on my dad. If it happened, it happened. There's nothing I can do to change the past. I also feel like I would remember it differently. Even though the memory is vivid and I can pinpoint exact details about the memory, it's only ever really resurfaced in my dreams. I never gave it much more thought than being an awful, awful dream till now. My other assault is haunting. It's not as vivid, but for a long time, it's all I thought about. I couldn't look in the mirror for months, I wasn't eating. It consumed nearly every waking thought I had for years. 

I don't know. I just don't know. I'm tearing myself apart over this. I just wanna lock it away and never think about it again, but now that I've really dug into it, I just can't stop. I feel like I'm crazy. I feel like I'm a crazy person who has just made something up out of nothing.  I hope it didn't happen. I hope I made it up. I really want to have made it up, but I just genuinely don't know. 

Sorry for the long post. I just needed to get this out somewhere. I don't know if this is the appropriate place for it, and please tell me if it's not, I'll put it somewhere else or get rid of it. I just needed to tell someone, and I needed to say it somewhere safe where people won't think I've gone insane or end up ruining my relationships.

parent_comment:
Thank you very much for your kind & considerate words. I don't mind the length of the text, but I appreciate you took the time to read my story as well, reacted to it & shared additional information. I thank you for your trust. I'm glad you recognized the truth, stopped blaming or telling yourself you deserved this and managed to see this guy for what he really was: an abuser who took advantage of your kindness & vulnerability.   


Indeed it seems there are a lot of similarities between our stories (unfortunately). Interestingly, just like in your case, I also felt safe with the perpetrator initially as he used to be a housemate & friend of one of my brothers - which is also one of the reasons I am too terrified to report him to the police. Not only do I feel uncomfortable to describe my SA experience to the police, the judges in the court and other strangers, I am also not comfortable with the idea that my family might find out about it as well, as my rapist tried to reach out to my brother to re-establish contact (I think my brother recognized at some point how toxic this person was - without me even mentioning the SA - and cut off ties with him just like me). I guess I am not as strong yet, unlike you, to open up about this to the important people in my life.  


So what can I say...it is nice to hear that you have supportive friends with whom you could share your trauma and they motivated you to report your rapist. title: Unpopular Opinion: I'm tired of hearing the whole "it's not your job to teach someone about XYZ"...
body:
I realize this will likely not be a popular post based on the number of times I see this phrase in the comments on this particular sub but I still wanted to share this, maybe controversial but ultimately, alternative view/thought process.

I hate willful ignorance probably more than anything, but being *"willfully ignorant of"* & just being *"ignorant of"* are different things. Some people grow up sheltered, privileged, unaware of the existence of prejudice or malice - They are ignorant in the sense that they don't yet know that another view, or experience, is different than their own. Willful ignorance however, is when someone knows those things but chooses to dismiss or ignore them altogether to remain close-minded. So when I see people say things like "It's not your job to teach your boyfriend about sexism" or "it's not your job to explain what privilege is to others" it bothers me because we were all ignorant of something, sometime in our life & if someone didn't teach us, we'd never know. I think it is our job, especially with those we're close with to at least try and help them understand something they may not be aware of. Now if the person does know & chooses to keep recognizing ONLY their experience, that's willful ignorance and it's not your job to "convince them" something merits consideration.

As an example, when I was around 18-19 I worked as a server/bartender and became good friends with this guy named Rocky. I should explain that I went to a small school (200 kids maybe) and it was almost completely white and I honestly had very little interaction with people from other races - which sucks btw - so there were a lot of things I didn't understand about the POC experience. Was I aware of racism? Yes, of course this is America but I didn't really understand the real life implications or experience of POC. Rocky was a black guy, and being friends with him was easy but I was constantly learning from him about his experience. One night we're working behind the bar together & this group comes in, they start ordering drinks but I also notice they keep calling Rocky, Tyrone. Now in my head I'm thinking they just can't see his name tag or maybe they misheard him, I'll correct them but when I do the guy just says "oh he your boyfriend or something?" I just said no, he's my friend & his name is Rocky but I realized this guy was *only* planning to respect Rocky if we were dating.

Later when the bar closed I asked Rocky what was up because I could see he was down. He explained how often that shit happened, where they'd use a "stereotypical black guy name" in a pejorative way unless a white person was around to give him "legitimacy". He told me about how these little things (micro-aggressions) had happened his whole life, how it affected him & his brothers. Rocky didn't have to share that with me, he could have taken the "it's not my job to explain racism to you" route but then I might never have understood micro-aggressions in the way I do now.

Yes I agree to some degree that it's every individuals responsibility to learn about how their experiences aren't shared by all, but I also think it's every one's job to help others who want to learn, understand them better. We don't all have the same experience and we don't all learn things at the same time so if it's not our job to help others understand, then whose job is it?

Really I guess this long rant is because I want to see more people sharing their experiences so we can understand them better and learn how to be better allies to each other. It would be amazing if people didn't need experiences like mine with Rocky to understand the weight of some things, but often it's just a lack of exposure and not willful ignorance.

**ETA: Due to the volume of messages attacking me, my husband and whatever minor semantics bothered people about this observation and request for more understanding I'm taking a break from the sub for a while. It's clear that while many are interested in using this forum for helping others understand women's perspectives, others are intent on using it to disparage others for simply not knowing something. I stand behind my statements.**

I can't let an opportunity go by for someone to be ignorant, but I also recognize it isn't my responsibility to educate everyone. I just worry about the outcome if I don't. She likened it to OCD.

title: I was raped but I don’t know what to feel. I’m confused
body:
Please read it all because I need help and advice
⚠️TW: SEXUAL ASSAULT AND SELF HARM⚠️ 

A few weeks ago I (19f) was raped by a guy I don’t know at a party. I was really drunk and didn’t consent to it happening but all I remember is being in the room and I was drugged. I remember him being on top of me and from then, I black out and I don’t remember anything that happened. He admitted to the police to having “consented sex” with me but I was unconscious and I didn’t consent so that’s just wild. But ever since it happened I’ve just felt so weird because I don’t remember anything so I don’t know if I’m supposed to be getting support or if I’m an actual victim or anything. But I’ll list all the things that have been happening to me so far since it’s happened.

Just to preface, I have autism and a semi BPD (borderline) diagnosis. My doctors have also spoken about me having an anxiety disorder.

•	⁠I’m finding it harder to sleep, so sometimes I won’t sleep for days at a time because I’m scared to sleep as when I do, I end up having night terrors or getting flashbacks. This leaves me waking up sweaty, with a racing heart, quick breathing, stressed and scared and often leads to a panic attack. I’ve had panic attacks before so this isn’t new but they do last a bit longer and during my panic attacks I feel like I can’t breathe and I pull at my hair.
•	⁠I can’t concentrate nor do I have the motivation to do anything anymore. I’m in university so I need to attend my lectures but I haven’t been in 2 going on to 3 weeks now and I’m very behind but I just can’t do my work. Nothing is registering in my brain and I feel stupid and like a failure because I’m so behind on everything.
•	⁠I’m losing motivation when it comes to my personal health and hygiene. I will lay in bed all day in the dark deep in thought or zoned out and I don’t brush my teeth or shower or eat any food. I can go 2-3 days without doing any of these but then I start feeling sick and like I’m going to pass out so I force myself to get in the shower and eat something. Even cooking and buying groceries is such a pain. I don’t want to do it anymore.
•	⁠Some days I’ll just feel numb and empty and like I’m living life on autopilot, almost like a robot and these days seem to be easier because I don’t feel anything. I’ll just feel disconnected from reality and my days feel like they’re blurring together. Other days I’m angry at everything, at my friends, at myself, at my situation and at my life. I just get angry and start crying and hitting myself in the head and want to self harm (cutting).
•	⁠Sometimes I feel like I can’t control my mind or my emotions I feel like I’m being taken over and I’ll just get so mad or so upset and start crying and having a breakdown, which less than often leads to a panic attack and sometimes leads to self harm where I’ll usually cut myself or hit/ punch myself in the head and throw things and after I’ll feel more depressed and annoyed with myself and regret what I did after.
•	⁠Nothing is fun anymore. I’ve been depressed since before I was a teenager and I could have my friends or hobbies as an escape but now I don’t want to talk to my friends, I don’t want to do my art or play my instrument or watch my shows or do anything. I wish I could disappear and be alone with a clear mind.
•	⁠I smoke weed and have for a few years as it helps me sleep at night and block/ slow down unwanted thoughts in my mind, but since I’ve been put on Sertraline/ Zoloft it’s made me really paranoid so I’ve had to quit smoking. But now I’m having more restless nights and I feel on edge and worried all the time and I just want to run far away.
•	⁠I feel like I don’t know what I’m doing with myself sometimes, almost unpredictable. A few nights ago, around 1am I was really down in the dumps and I just wanted to feel alive so I took a couple bumps of Ketamine and went on a bike ride in -3° weather. My fingers started going numb so I stopped to smoke some weed even though I was supposed to quit and smoked it but then I realised I didn’t know where I was since I started cycling randomly and I started panicking, broke down crying and just got an uber home.
•	⁠When I speak to someone or I’m in my lecture or on the bus I often zone out and forget what’s being said or what’s going on around me and I have to focus extra hard. I feel out of it and like I’m not processing what’s going on around me.
•	⁠I tried to take my own life about a week after it happened and I got sent to the psych ward but I was released after two days. Then they gave me antidepressants and I’ve been taking them for a week.
•	⁠I started self harming again after being clean for months and I don’t know why, maybe I just wanted to feel something again? I keep getting thoughts of wanting to self harm and end my life cause I feel like there’s no point of anything anymore and nothing even matters.
•	⁠When I try opening up to my friend they keep being strange and annoying. For example, people who know about the situation will ask them how I’m doing if I’m not around since we live near, and they will come to me and tell me that people asked about me and they will be like “What about me?! Why are they not asking how I’m doing?!” and it annoys me and throws me off cause it’s not really about you right now you know. Maybe I’m being selfish. When I express how I’m feeling, be this depressed or like I don’t wanna be here anymore, they will start complaining about things in their life and saying how the fact that I’m depressed is making them depressed and if I did anything to myself they wouldn’t be able to live and then I’d have to comfort them and it’s just kind of strange, like it’s a depression olympics or something. I try not to think about it too deeply cause they’re my friend but it annoys the hell out of me and so I don’t like opening up to them anymore cause it’s always weird. Not to say they can’t open up to me, they always can but they only do it when I do it so that’s why I feel like it’s weird.

I just feel alone because I can’t tell anyone how I’m feeling. I don’t have any friends or family who I’m close enough to open up to, and the only people that I think I can I don’t feel comfortable telling them all this cause what can they do for me? I guess this was a huge rant and stuff I needed to get off my chest and see if people can help me with what’s going on in my mind and any advice would be helpful. I’ve tried talking therapy in the past but that was awful I’ll never do that again so anything else would be appreciated.
parent_comment:
I wanna start by saying that I’m so sorry that you went through that. I wish I could just give you a hug. 
I have experienced many of the things you are now, five years ago when I was 14. After having five years to heal, here is what I will tell you. Time will heal, I know that doesn’t help you to hear now, but I want you to know that the nightmares and the panic will become less intense over time and eventually go away. 
It will be important to address your trauma but that is after your mental health is stable once again. 
I’m not sure if your school was made aware of the situation since you mentioned the police were but I would send your teachers an email, I know it seems extremely intimidating but the sooner you address it, the easier it will be. You are not a failure at all. I hope you can give yourself love and grace, because you needed to give yourself some time. 
Maybe making a check list of the things you need to do for the day could help. It can help you to feel more accomplished and motivated. 
Could you order groceries online and have them delivered? and maybe get some food that’s easy to prepare while you are still healing. 
I’m sorry your friends haven’t supported you in the way that you have needed. It’s invalidating for a friend to bring up their issues while talking about yours and it’s important for a friend to listen. 
I’d imagine a lot of things feel out of control right now, but when someone self harms, they are in control, and that’s what makes it more tempting. 
I know you mentioned you don’t like therapy but I did EMDR therapy, and it’s a process of revisiting and healing from the situation. It sucked going through it but it honestly changed my life so I just wanted to put it out there. I have also been through quite a few mental health programs, and would love to send you some skills I’ve learned if you are interested. I honestly just wanna help you in anyway I can. I’m sending you so much love. I hope something in this message helps ❣️

title: Feeling like I’m overreacting
body:
I totally feel like I’m overreacting and maybe looking for some validation and support, especially since I haven’t really been vocal about this in my real life with my friends. I’ve recently started to explore this in therapy, but my difficulty with sexual intimacy is really frustrating, especially as a newlywed in her late-20’s. 

TW

5 years ago, I went on a first date with a guy, and I’m not sure why, but I was like why don’t we just go to your place and hang out. We get there and are hanging out and put on a movie, and we start making out, which I was 100% comfortable with. He keeps trying to push further and further, and I think I tried to maintain my boundary of kissing is all I’m comfortable with. A lot of the details are fuzzy, and I’m not sure if it’s because 5 years has passed or otherwise. Anyway, we’re making out and he keeps trying to take it further and further and then he said something along the lines of “well you came here, what did you expect would happen?” After he said this and because of all the asking and suggesting, I remember just kind of giving in and having sex with him. I don’t remember a good chunk of the actual sex except for when he choked me (put his hand around my neck and applied a bit of pressure, nothing crazy, but definitely not chill). I remember after getting up and checking my phone and thinking wtf did I do? And then I don’t have much of a recollection beyond that. But again... 5 years has gone by. 

I really struggle with this, especially because it’s not clear cut assault to me because in my mind, I DID go over there. I didn’t say no. I went along with it. I hung out with him a handful of times after that and willingly had sex with him. But when I was seeing him after, I ALWAYS wanted this guy’s approval. I don’t know why. He made me so anxious because I just wanted him to like me for some dumb reason. 

Anyway, some validation/insight/etc. Would be really appreciated ❤️

parent_comment:
You’re not overreacting. Your feelings are valid. And your experience of that night is not invalidated by your hanging out with him afterwards, that is actually pretty common. A lot of us do this because we’re trying to normalize what just happened, make it not what it was. Everything I say here I say as a survivor myself, so please know there is no judgement, only understanding. 

It is clear to me, from his refusal to take no for an answer to his saying “you came here, what did you expect” that that dude is an absolute predator. You know what SHOULD happen in sexual encounters? Enthusiastic consent. We do not have a right to each other’s bodies. It is not the responsibility of women to ward off the unwanted sexual advances of men. It is the responsibility of each party to ensure that the other is enthusiastically consenting and totally on board before we go about inserting things into their body. Also, choking during sex should absolutely be discussed and agreed to beforehand. It is NOT something any person should feel comfortable just *doing* without prior consent.

This guy did not care if you enjoyed the experience. He only cared about himself. So many men do not have sex with women, they masturbate using use women’s bodies. It’s not a shared experience between two humans, it’s a physical sensation for them. And this is A Problem. This is date rape culture. 

Can you imagine for a second being him? Pushing someone into something they’re clearly not into? Can you imagine how little you would have to care about them to do such a thing? How selfish you would have to be?

You are not overreacting. What you experienced was sexual assault. Those who say otherwise  are amongst the predators. And you are not at fault for what he did. 

I’ve found therapy and connecting with other women who understand to be really helpful. Fuck this guy, and all men who think this behavior is okay. Women all over the world are are finding our voices and calling out these men who have so long benefitted from our silence. Join us.

title: At which point can something be considered rape?
body:
Edit: To everyone who took her/his/their time to answer to my post: Thank you so much! I cried a lot, but despite that, you gave me very valuable input and a lot to think about.

&#x200B;

My husband (m34) and i (f30) don't have a lot of sex, due to other problems in our relationship. I am the "problematic one" there, meaning i am the one who doesn't  want to sleep with him, or better, i somehow can't. It's not some kind  of revenge from my side, it just doesn't feel right for me, when there  is so much else that needs resolve first (i know that some people might  see it in a different way, and that's perfectly fine!).

We also went to a  therapist, to which we don't go anymore after my husband said that it  wasn't worth anything, because we still don't sleep with each other more often... . There was a time when he was very abusive to me (verbally, the  reason was not the lack of sex, and he was very controlling, taking away  my card of our bankaccount, etc.), basically telling me i was a  worthless piece of sh\*t, and i think this contributed to my feeling of  not feeling safe around him to relax enough to become intimate again. I really tried to come over it and forget it, but even after 2 years it stuck and my mind can't process it. He also has a  caring and nice side though, so it is not like every day is hell, so maybe i should be happy, at the same time it makes things just more complicated.

It didn't help that up until recently, my husbands opinion always  had been that in our relationship the only problem is the lack of sex,  and that maybe i should seek professional help, giving me all  responsibility. I felt wrong and guilty all the time, and somehow still  do, although something in my mind tells me that this thought is also not correct.

So, after this little bit of context, here is what happened and why i am asking:

One afternoon when we were alone, my husband started kissing and  touching me. When he started to undress me i told him that i don't want  to sleep with him, he continued, and i didn't say anything anymore. He  was already hard and touched me a little bit more, until it seemed as if  he wanted to enter me, and again i tensed and said "no", not in a loud  angry voice, but it didn't sound playful/flirty either. I tried to pull  up my pants, and he stopped me and told me i should wait, just wait, and  then penetrated me. I just felt numb and didn't push him off or  anything, after some thrusts the doorbell rang and disrupted what was  happening. Afterwards i went into our bedroom and cried a lot and i don't even really know why, i felt awful for the rest of the day.  When i was still sad in the evening my husband got really angry,  because i said that i felt terrible because of what had happened (I said  sth. like "because of what you did!"), and he almost yelled: "What  do you think it was? Huh? Huh?", to which i just replied: "I said no  and you still did it...".

Weeks, some months, went by, and we haven't slept with each other  since then, he also didn't try to again, and i still try to figure out  what that was. I told two of my closest friends about it, and they said  that it was basically rape, but somehow some part of me doesn't want to  believe it, i feel ashamed and embarrassed, and some naive romantic part  of me tells me that it couldn't have been rape because we are married  and he is my husband, or that it's my own fault because i didn't say no  vehemently enough, that i should have fought back more.

I don't trust my  gut-feeling at all and find it very difficult to distinguish between me  overreacting or making a victim out of myself and feeling "rightfully"  hurt. Or is it an absolutely individual thing and up to oneself to set  boundaries?

I feel so bad about everything and don't really know why.

I am sorry if this is not the right subforum. If that is the case i  would be very happy if you gave me some advice where posting this is  more appropriate. Furthermore, i am also sorry for mistakes and/or bad  grammar, english isn't my first language :|.

Thank you so much for reading.
parent_comment:
The only problem here is him. You did not cause this. Even if it were possible for you to create circumstances to allow him to think this was okay, first he had to be okay with having sex with you without your consent. He knew you didn't want to. He felt entitled to your body, that's all. 

Maybe that's why you have no desire to have sex with him. Your body knows this guy can't be trusted. There's nothing wrong with you.

title: I understand now
body:
A few months ago, I was r*ped. 

Before this happened, I had been sexually assaulted by a past partner of mine, but I didn’t feel as ashamed about it because I was asleep when it happened. The only thing I felt bad about was calling it what it was, because I didn’t want to say it happened to me. I never thought it could.

Before a few months ago, I didn’t understand how people couldn’t talk about being r*ped or when they didn’t want to report it. It’s not that I shamed them, because it’s a traumatic experience and everyone deals with things differently, but I just didn’t think I’d be that person if it happened to me. Boy was I wrong.

I grew up in an extremely Christian household, so sex before marriage is very taboo. I would feel a little more comfortable telling my family if it didn’t happen the way it did. 

A partner that I had previously had consented to did this to me. Someone I trusted. What makes me feel even worse is that I had originally consented to sex that night. However, when I told him I wanted to use protection, and told him no when he begged, he still did it. I didn’t know what to do, so I just went along with it so nothing worse would happen. 

I feel horrible calling it what it is. My brain has convinced me that because I didn’t throw him off of me or that I had sex with him again even the same night (I hadn’t completely processed what happened), that it wasn’t r*pe. I feel completely horrible and alone.

Today, I had to fill out a jury questionnaire because I was summoned. One of the questions is “Have you or someone close to you been a victim of a crime?” Originally, I put no. Then I realized that wasn’t the truth and that it’s illegal to lie on forms like that, but then when I changed it and put yes, I felt like I wasn’t telling the truth either, because my situation isn’t cut and dry. 

I don’t want to press charges and I don’t want anyone to know. My boyfriend and best friend are the only two people that know, and that’s very hard. I just don’t feel comfortable sharing with everyone else.

title: Unpopular Opinion: I'm tired of hearing the whole "it's not your job to teach someone about XYZ"...
body:
I realize this will likely not be a popular post based on the number of times I see this phrase in the comments on this particular sub but I still wanted to share this, maybe controversial but ultimately, alternative view/thought process.

I hate willful ignorance probably more than anything, but being *"willfully ignorant of"* & just being *"ignorant of"* are different things. Some people grow up sheltered, privileged, unaware of the existence of prejudice or malice - They are ignorant in the sense that they don't yet know that another view, or experience, is different than their own. Willful ignorance however, is when someone knows those things but chooses to dismiss or ignore them altogether to remain close-minded. So when I see people say things like "It's not your job to teach your boyfriend about sexism" or "it's not your job to explain what privilege is to others" it bothers me because we were all ignorant of something, sometime in our life & if someone didn't teach us, we'd never know. I think it is our job, especially with those we're close with to at least try and help them understand something they may not be aware of. Now if the person does know & chooses to keep recognizing ONLY their experience, that's willful ignorance and it's not your job to "convince them" something merits consideration.

As an example, when I was around 18-19 I worked as a server/bartender and became good friends with this guy named Rocky. I should explain that I went to a small school (200 kids maybe) and it was almost completely white and I honestly had very little interaction with people from other races - which sucks btw - so there were a lot of things I didn't understand about the POC experience. Was I aware of racism? Yes, of course this is America but I didn't really understand the real life implications or experience of POC. Rocky was a black guy, and being friends with him was easy but I was constantly learning from him about his experience. One night we're working behind the bar together & this group comes in, they start ordering drinks but I also notice they keep calling Rocky, Tyrone. Now in my head I'm thinking they just can't see his name tag or maybe they misheard him, I'll correct them but when I do the guy just says "oh he your boyfriend or something?" I just said no, he's my friend & his name is Rocky but I realized this guy was *only* planning to respect Rocky if we were dating.

Later when the bar closed I asked Rocky what was up because I could see he was down. He explained how often that shit happened, where they'd use a "stereotypical black guy name" in a pejorative way unless a white person was around to give him "legitimacy". He told me about how these little things (micro-aggressions) had happened his whole life, how it affected him & his brothers. Rocky didn't have to share that with me, he could have taken the "it's not my job to explain racism to you" route but then I might never have understood micro-aggressions in the way I do now.

Yes I agree to some degree that it's every individuals responsibility to learn about how their experiences aren't shared by all, but I also think it's every one's job to help others who want to learn, understand them better. We don't all have the same experience and we don't all learn things at the same time so if it's not our job to help others understand, then whose job is it?

Really I guess this long rant is because I want to see more people sharing their experiences so we can understand them better and learn how to be better allies to each other. It would be amazing if people didn't need experiences like mine with Rocky to understand the weight of some things, but often it's just a lack of exposure and not willful ignorance.

**ETA: Due to the volume of messages attacking me, my husband and whatever minor semantics bothered people about this observation and request for more understanding I'm taking a break from the sub for a while. It's clear that while many are interested in using this forum for helping others understand women's perspectives, others are intent on using it to disparage others for simply not knowing something. I stand behind my statements.**

title: I feel failed by everyone.
body:
tw: sa, I will go slightly into detail since I just need to let it all out tbh


I got assaulted last year by a "friend" I had known for about 3 months prior to that. He went to the same grade as I did, we had quite a few classes together and we hung out together during our breaks. 
I think it was more so because I would've felt bad to reject him and he seemed nice enough, even though he had some really extreme political views about women and bodily autonomy (he was a really strict catholic).

It got really weird at some point since he clung to me, followed me around etc and just didn't leave me alone, came way too close.  
He made advances and unsolicited sexual "jokes" (for example when I played a song with a little more explicit lyrics he'd ask whether or not I want to tell him something, or when I just said anything remotely sexual he'd ask the same thing). I rejected him every single time.
He knew I'm asexual and sex repulsed.

We met up two times outside of school, one time we went to the next bigger city, the other time we went for a picnic with my dog. 
We were out and about for maybe 5 hours before going back to my home, exhausted as fuck as you can imagine. 

I have a couch for two people, but lying down only one can really fit on there. 
I lay down, and he just squeezed himself behind me, wrapping his arms around me, which I found to be kind of inappropriate but whatever, I was honestly too tired to say something.
I just wanted to nap.

After some time, he started humping me from behind. I froze. I didn't know what to do, I didn't know what was even happening. I thought maybe he was spasming in his sleep or something, since it wasn't like.. fast.
Idk. 
I just wanted it to be over. It took maybe 10-20 minutes, I don't even know for sure. 
He wrapped his leg around me before suddenly standing up and saying he was putting me in a compromising position. 

Afterwards he left. 

It took me almost a month to fully process everything and finally file a police report for sexual harassment since I wasn't even sure if it would count as sexual assault. 
Filing the report was already humiliating enough. They told me my mom couldn't be there if she was meant to be a witness in court. 
A guy questioned me in his office which he shared with someone else. That someone was there, just working on unrelated things. 
He asked me so many questions, about where he touched me, how he touched me, if i think he came etc. 

A month ago I got a letter. 
They closed the proceedings. 

Why?
Well, firstly because of the lack of evidence, which I understand, but it's still stupid. How is there supposed to be evidence if he does it when no ones there and he doesn't actually undress/undress me. 
It was basically a he-said-they-said-case.

But then they went on about how he seemed apologetic and didn't even know he did something wrong, and how I knew we would be close in proximity when allowing him on the couch, and also how I didn't say no even though I didn't have to, legally.
They were degrading.
They were outright victim blaming. 

I understand that they can't do much without evidence, but victim blaming is just so bad. 

I wanted to write a letter to them but it wouldn't have changed a thing, plus I had to go to the hospital suddenly so I couldn't have even written and sent it there in time. 

It still hurts, every single day. 
There were so many red flags, but they just seemed to be cultural differences (he was an exchange student), so I chalked it up to that. Hell, even my father (prior to the incident) excused it with cultural differences. 

For example, he wanted to hug me. I told him no. He did it anyway. 
He's against tattoos, piercings, abortions, even if the person in question got raped. I tried to argue with him, but he just went on and on and on with the same arguments, which he seemed to do a lot. He was really self absorbed and I hated it. 
I actually wanted to end the friendship prior to everything happening but firstly, I felt bad and guilty, and secondly he would've been gone in a few months anyway. 

After I reported the incident, the school banned him for the entirety of two days before being like "yeah, he can come in again".
He didn't come. Why? Because he was "disappointed in the school".

I opened up to a (male) friend who also is in the same grade as I am, so he knew the guy in question. 
He accused me of being a Karen, and I had to explain to him in detail what he did and how long it took etc just so he'd stop.

I feel failed. By me, by him, by the school, by my "friend", by the police/law enforcement. 

I just want it to be over. 


I'm sorry for it being that long, and thank you for listening to my rant. I had to let it out somewhere.
parent_comment:
I'm so sorry that the people who were supposed to help you and the people you trusted enough to open up to turned around and victim-blamed and did not believe you or the severity. 

I am so sorry they told you that you would've known that you both would be close. That is just so, so wrong. That's like telling a victim of a robbery that it was their fault because they were carrying their wallet in front of who they should have known was a robber. You were literally just living your life when *he* chose to do this. You are so right when you say what they said was degrading. 

And I am so sorry that they chalked this guy off to "not knowing" and being "apologetic." First of all, he literally said "I'm putting you in a compromising position," so obviously he knew (and he still knew even if he hadn't said that). But whether or not he had said anything at all, I am astounded (though not surprised) that the police told you that this guy - who literally committed the action - did "not know" yet you - a victim - were supposed to know what you were getting into?!?! WTF?! And then to top it off, they say he's "apologetic" as if that absolves him from everything. I am so, so sorry.

It sounds like you recognize that this was not your fault, which is a recognition that is already difficult to make with SA but is even more difficult when there are people around you telling you that you had responsibility for this. I hope you are seeing the strength and courage you have in recognizing and accepting the truth that it is not your fault in spite of what others tell you.

I have experienced something similar in being victim-blamed, seeing the red flags before the assault, and the guy who assaulted me being allowed to continue his education at the same school as me. Though it is still painful to remember and acknowledge, it does get better. There is hope that you will feel okay and the burden of this experience will not weigh so heavily on you. 

Also from personal experiences, I want to say - be careful who you share details with. I learned the hard way that "friends" (both guy and girl friends) would not *say* they believed me until I shared details for the following reason: they actually did know that it happened, but they wanted details to either gossip or to know for their own sick, depraved curiosity. I'm not saying that this friend of yours had the same intentions as mine did, but you might run into someone later who does, so be careful.

If someone - especially a friend - does not believe you, the burden of proof does not rest on you for them to become convinced it happened. If he really knew you as a friend, the burden of proof lies on him to recognize that you are not someone who is or has been a "Karen" or as someone who overreacts. But I think you know that.

My response is also really long haha I hope something from this helps you. Take care, and I wish the best for you.

title: Does this count as coercion?
body:
I'm sorry for adding to the list of "was this sexual assault" questions but I am going out of my mind here trying to figure out if I am overreacting or being overdramatic.  I am totally lost and just need some objective outside perspective.  

I was hanging out with a friend in his room playing video games when he started to get really physically affectionate (grabbing me for a hug, pulling me closer and holding me there, etc). I kept just pulling back and laughing it off but eventually he suddenly pulled me down and started kissing me.  I completely froze and was nervous about upsetting him so I went with it until I could find an out.  He asked to have sex and I told him no, and then he asked again for "just a few seconds" and I told him no again and offered something else like oral hoping he would stop. But he kept trying to penetrate completely unprotected and it eventually got to the point where he was on top of me and I was physically covering myself with my hands to keep him out.  He asked me a third time, but it was only asking if I wanted him to go get a condom or not, and at that point I figured he was going to do it anyway and this was my chance to at least make sure it was safe.  I'm sure I acted like I was enjoying it because I tried to convince myself that I was and that everything was fine, but every other thought was "I really don't want to be doing this" or "I want this to be over."

Was this coercion? My therapist said it qualifies as assault but I don't know.  All I know is that I had told him before that I wasn't interested in a relationship with him and that I spent the whole time wanting to leave but being too worried of his reaction if I tried. We are both mid/late 20s if that helps.
parent_comment: That's where everybody starts out. The rose colored glasses that make the world seem safe are ever present. Then, one day they crack and the real world becomes much harder to ignore. That sudden jerk from the everyday to what feels like a battlefield or maybe even a horror film/action movie takes a while to catch up with you. It's all so confusing and disorienting. What's safe? What was really a red flag we couldn't see through the rosey tint of the glasses? How do we fit into this new more dangerous world? How do we avoid it happening again? If bad things happen to bad people then am I bad? Or is the world callous and random and these kinds of things are just unavoidable and completely at the mercy of luck? How dangerous is the new world now that we're in it? Is it as dangerous as it seems or am I just on hypervigilance mode all the time now? There's a lot to manage when the realization sticks and not much of it is very fun. Especially when you have a fear response or your body betrays your mind and parts of the assault feel good. All of that just confuses things way worse. The good/bad news is, you're not alone. Many people have gone through this before you, many have gone through it after you, and many more will go through it one day. Each and every last one of those people can help you to sort things out if and when you're comfortable enough to ask a question. I've been around the block enough times myself that I generally have at least some idea how to help or what other's are going through and there's never any judgement on my part. And if you're not comfortable with asking me or taking my advice specifically there's a couple thousand people on here to help you out. It's rough, but you'll make it through to the other side. Have a great week and a fantastic new year.

Do not take this lightly. You get to decide what your boundaries are and when you do that, when you respect your own personal space, you set an example for your boyfriend and your two best girlfriends. title: Unpopular Opinion: I'm tired of hearing the whole "it's not your job to teach someone about XYZ"...
body:
I realize this will likely not be a popular post based on the number of times I see this phrase in the comments on this particular sub but I still wanted to share this, maybe controversial but ultimately, alternative view/thought process.

I hate willful ignorance probably more than anything, but being *"willfully ignorant of"* & just being *"ignorant of"* are different things. Some people grow up sheltered, privileged, unaware of the existence of prejudice or malice - They are ignorant in the sense that they don't yet know that another view, or experience, is different than their own. Willful ignorance however, is when someone knows those things but chooses to dismiss or ignore them altogether to remain close-minded. So when I see people say things like "It's not your job to teach your boyfriend about sexism" or "it's not your job to explain what privilege is to others" it bothers me because we were all ignorant of something, sometime in our life & if someone didn't teach us, we'd never know. I think it is our job, especially with those we're close with to at least try and help them understand something they may not be aware of. Now if the person does know & chooses to keep recognizing ONLY their experience, that's willful ignorance and it's not your job to "convince them" something merits consideration.

As an example, when I was around 18-19 I worked as a server/bartender and became good friends with this guy named Rocky. I should explain that I went to a small school (200 kids maybe) and it was almost completely white and I honestly had very little interaction with people from other races - which sucks btw - so there were a lot of things I didn't understand about the POC experience. Was I aware of racism? Yes, of course this is America but I didn't really understand the real life implications or experience of POC. Rocky was a black guy, and being friends with him was easy but I was constantly learning from him about his experience. One night we're working behind the bar together & this group comes in, they start ordering drinks but I also notice they keep calling Rocky, Tyrone. Now in my head I'm thinking they just can't see his name tag or maybe they misheard him, I'll correct them but when I do the guy just says "oh he your boyfriend or something?" I just said no, he's my friend & his name is Rocky but I realized this guy was *only* planning to respect Rocky if we were dating.

Later when the bar closed I asked Rocky what was up because I could see he was down. He explained how often that shit happened, where they'd use a "stereotypical black guy name" in a pejorative way unless a white person was around to give him "legitimacy". He told me about how these little things (micro-aggressions) had happened his whole life, how it affected him & his brothers. Rocky didn't have to share that with me, he could have taken the "it's not my job to explain racism to you" route but then I might never have understood micro-aggressions in the way I do now.

Yes I agree to some degree that it's every individuals responsibility to learn about how their experiences aren't shared by all, but I also think it's every one's job to help others who want to learn, understand them better. We don't all have the same experience and we don't all learn things at the same time so if it's not our job to help others understand, then whose job is it?

Really I guess this long rant is because I want to see more people sharing their experiences so we can understand them better and learn how to be better allies to each other. It would be amazing if people didn't need experiences like mine with Rocky to understand the weight of some things, but often it's just a lack of exposure and not willful ignorance.

**ETA: Due to the volume of messages attacking me, my husband and whatever minor semantics bothered people about this observation and request for more understanding I'm taking a break from the sub for a while. It's clear that while many are interested in using this forum for helping others understand women's perspectives, others are intent on using it to disparage others for simply not knowing something. I stand behind my statements.**
parent_comment:
One of the reasons I still engage in reddit debates (even though I feel like it ages me sometimes) is because I know that people ARE reading the posts and I might be able to just get 1 person to think differently, then it's worth it.

I used to be stubborn and bull headed and set in my beliefs. Raised conservative, I would try to convert my school friends to the republican party as early as 15 years old. It took YEARS and loving people to talk to me like a human about all the issues I was so sure about and show me that most of my beliefs were wrong. 

If those same people have said "go do your own research it's not my job to teach you why you're wrong" I would have ended up just joining the Young Americans group in college where all the Republicans were and kept my ideology the same. 

Yeah, it's a lot more effort to show someone why their experiences aren't the end all be all. Yeah you're probably not gonna see the long term consequences of what you did. But you might actually change people's minds.

Telling someone to do their own research will just end up with someone in the Google echo chamber they were already in.

title: Assaulted at 15 by someone I trusted.
body:
30 M. Seeing so many brave souls step forward and speak of their experiences has given me the strength to tell my story in full. I was 15 years old when I was assaulted. I was a virgin, and I was wrestling a lot with my identity and my sexuality at that time. I’m autistic, so I have a very difficult time connecting with people, and back then when “friends” and sex were everything, I suppose I was especially vulnerable. I was socially awkward, lonely, and highly impressionable which made me very easy to manipulate. If somebody, anybody, gave me the time of day, I imprinted immediately and trusted them implicitly. I didn’t have very much interest in sex, even at that age, but peer pressure ultimately pushed me to seek something that I wasn’t fully comfortable with and I ended up in the arms of my abuser. We were over at her place, in the upstairs game room, when she started making moves on me. At first I went along with it because I trusted her, and because I was a teenage boy. It’s what I was “supposed” to do, but I quickly realized when she slid her hand down the front of my pants that I wasn’t comfortable with what was happening and I told her to stop, but she didn’t and I froze. 

She coerced, and even belittled me as she undressed me from the waist down- saying things like: “It’s fine. Don’t be a bitch.” And despite my continued verbal protests, she climbed into my lap. From there she used me until she achieved climax and then hardly even acknowledged me for the rest of my time there. It’s very apparent to me now that my “No”, who I was as a person, and my needs meant nothing to her. To her I was nothing more than a tool of pleasure, and like the stupid kid that I was at the time, I kept going back because I was a teenage boy. I was “supposed” to have sex, she “loved me” and I didn’t want to lose her. So I kept thinking maybe it would be different next time. Next time. Next time, but it was always the same and by that point I had either allowed her to convince me, or, more likely, had convinced myself that that was how it was supposed to be. I didn’t want it, but my needs didn’t matter. Just lay there and take it like a good boy. Eventually I was able to break free from her, but at that age, I lacked the capacity to understand what really happened. So the idea that I’d been raped multiple times never even crossed my mind. I’d done what I was “supposed” to do. I met a girl. I had sex. So I just let it go and moved on. But after I got away, something wasn’t right in my head. My sense of self-worth, my idea of sexuality, and my trust in others- especially women, were all badly shaken. 

I developed a serious drinking problem and I had this deep sense of loathing of myself and of women that I could not explain, and it was only recently, after a couple years of sobriety and the clarity that it brought, that I realized what happened to me when I was young, and that that moment played a huge part in why I was who I was and why I am who I am now. And it devastated me. I tried to minimize my own pain, sanitize my own story to make it go away. Tried to tell myself: “It wasn’t that bad. Sack up and be a man.” I even almost turned back to drinking because killing the memory or myself seemed like the better option…

It took a long time for me to admit to myself that I was raped, because I kept telling myself: “You said ‘no’, but you were aroused.” “You said ‘stop’, but you made no efforts to remove her from you. On some level you must have wanted it. Otherwise you wouldn’t have been aroused and you would have fought harder to get away from her. And you certainly wouldn’t have kept going back.” But I’ve come to realize that arousal does not mean desire and that compliance does not mean consent. What the body wants and what the mind wants can be two totally different things and if the body says “yes” that doesn’t mean the mind does. Now I’m trying to untangle nearly 12 years of alcoholism, depression and repressed trauma piece by piece in an attempt to make sense of, and come to peace with, my past. I’m hoping that telling my story will bring me one step closer to being able to do so. 

Thank you all so much for your bravery, and thank you for listening.

title: Was this sexual assault?

And he said that he felt a connection with me and like he could talk to me but he didn’t feel that way with others. He asked me if I felt that too and I gave a halfway response like “yeah, yeah I feel like I can talk to you” or something to that effect, but I was uncomfortable. And then he started talking about how he wished he could kiss me, and I immediately said how that would be an absolutely horrible idea because I love my boyfriend, who was in the other room, and my friendship with his brother was very important to me. And then he kept pushing, and I just kept giving variations of the same answer. At some point he goes wait, I should probably… and then he gets up and closes the door. I’m not sure if he locked it. And he comes back and he keeps asking to kiss me, and as he says this he is blocking my passage to the door. In my drunken state, I was still very concerned about getting back to clean up the spill. So I was eager to leave, even on top of all of the uncomfortability. He implied that if I kissed him I could leave. And I again explained why I didn’t want to do that. Then he said something to the effect of “well if I kiss you, it won’t be your fault” and started kissing me.

This is where I don’t have any more memory for a bit, until I heard a noise outside of the room and realized I didn’t have clothes on, and I freaked out and told him to stop and got up and started getting dressed. I cannot remember what I said. Around midnight, he called me several times which my boyfriend found odd and then came back over. I was asleep on the couch with my boyfriend, but then Jim came and sat on the couch and stared at me for a good 5 minutes, and rubbed my head for a second, and obviously this weirded my bf out. Then Jim went upstairs, and asked me to go upstairs as well (over text), which I didn’t see, but I did go upstairs to use the bathroom, and my boyfriend didn’t even feel comfortable letting me go to the bathroom while this guy was there, even though he didn’t know what had happened yet. Eventually, the guy left.

My drunkenness started to wear off at some point during the early morning, and I was starting to realize what had happened, but I wasn’t exactly sure. Eventually, Jim came over in the morning to clean his brother’s sheets because of what had happened. I hadn’t really processed everything that was going on, and he is a few years younger than me, so I felt very, very guilty about what had happened and I apologized to him for being so drunk, as I have more of a responsibility to control my alcohol intake. He seemed pretty regretful of what had happened at first, and I told him that I didn’t remember exactly the extent of what we had done, but I did remember frantically putting my clothes back on, etc. It was pretty awkward for a bit, and he explained to me that we did have sex. His story lined up pretty similarly with mine, save for a few details, and when he talked about how he was asking to kiss me, he said “Now this is where I feel bad because I feel like I pushed it a little bit, I’m sorry”, and he continued telling me what happened.

Throughout the conversation, he made several jokes like “It finally happened” and “we should do it again” and was talking about how he had seen me naked. He also started talking about how good it was and told me it was the best he had had because I “made noises” which made me feel absolutely disgusting obviously. He asked me if I thought it was good, and I told him I didn’t remember it. He told me that it was good for me because I apparently “came” and he had to “keep me quiet”. I have NEVER in my ENTIRE life came from penetrative sex alone. He also said that when he had come back over that night, it was because he wanted to do more. 

He asked me if I planned to tell anyone. I felt absolutely horrible and I told him that I had to tell my boyfriend. He didn’t like the idea of that, and I felt bad because he was younger than me and he visits his brother (who lives with my bf) all the time and I didn’t want to ruin that. I told him I would try to think of a way to tell him that wouldn’t damage his relationship with his brother. I couldn’t understand why I would have possibly done this, because I had never, EVER once in my life been attracted to him, and I feel so disgusted with myself. He really emphasized that I don’t tell anyone, and he said he wouldn’t tell anyone either, even his brother. I told him if he needed to talk to someone about what had happened, he could tell his brother, but I would want to know first. He said he wouldn’t tell anyone ever. Fast forward to the next morning, and I get a text from my friend, who is the older brother of Jim, in a groupchat with his gf and a mutual friend of ours saying that they knew what I had done, that they had already heard Jim’s story, and even though I had “asked him to keep it on the DL”, I needed to tell my boyfriend.

I had always planned to tell my boyfriend, so I don’t know what he told them. And I also thought it was odd that he begged me not to tell anyone and then told all of our mutual friends. I talked to my friend (Jim’s brother) about it and he said he’s not sure who to believe because our stories are different and his brother was telling everyone I initiated it. But he said he wasn’t mad at me and he wasn’t there so he couldn’t say for sure “who was lying”. But now he’s gone and removed me from every social media platform and blocked me, among other things.

Luckily, my bf believes me about what happened, but I still feel very, very guilty about my role in this. Obviously, I wish I hadn’t been as drunk, because then none of this probably would’ve happened. But I’m worried that somewhere during that time, I gave the impression that I wanted what was happening or I had consented in some way. I NEVER would’ve thought this person would do something like this… I guess that’s why my brain missed all of the warning signals. I feel so stupid for allowing it to go that far and I want to know if what I’m feeling is just deep regret or if I was adamant enough in saying no. I don’t understand why I didn’t immediately tell someone what had happened or why I even spoke to him the next day. And Jim, according to our mutual friends, is “devastated” and everyone is really worried about him. I feel absolutely insane and I just want to know if I’m a bad person or if this was what I think it was… or some combination of the two. If you made it this far… thank you for your help  :(

You were drunk, but thats not a crime, why should you not be able to get drunk in an environment you thought you were safe in. He has abused that drunkenness and abused you in the worst possible way. Putting the blame on the victim might restore their illusion of control (admitting that sometimes we do not have control over a situation is a scary and too unpleasant thought). title: I went in to get an ultrasound and I left with an IUD without my explicit consent
body:
Long story short, I went to the gynecologic with the intention of getting myself checked out and asking about birth control. I left with an IUD in tears.

Long story:

At the start of the visit (that was about 20 minutes) the doctor told me that the pills I wanted wouldn't be a great fit because of my weight. I said okay, in my mind thinking that then I wouldn't get anything. I had never been on hormones and I was a little scared of the possible mood swings and such. This was also my second ever trip to the gynecologist and I was really nervous.

She asked me if I had considered a contraceptive implant or an IUD, but I said that I was scared of them both because I wouldn't be able to get them out myself.

She just said that I should think it over and that she'd be able to put the IUD in right now. I said that I was scared of the pain, so if it would hurt a lot to put it in, then I don't want it. I said that I had read horror stories about it. She didn't really say anything to that, and we started the examination.

In the end, there was nothing wrong, and then I'm not completely sure what happened next because of the shock and the pain. Suddenly she's opening the box and inserting the IUD and I kind of blacked out, I know I was screaming and it was absolute hell. The worst pain of my life. I didn't even take a painkiller before because I didn't know it was going to happen.

The nurse that was by my head (I guess there to keep me calm) was also kind of chuckling and commenting that my eyes were really wide and telling me to breathe. I guess trauma is funny. They did keep asking me if I was okay, but I was in shock and just said yes, I guess.

So the doctor didn't really explain anything about the IUD (I know how it works since I've researched it but she didn't know that) and didn't really get my consent to put it in either. I didn't explicitly say no, but I think she should have made sure? She also kept asking me if I felt like she was pressuring me, and I think that it was sign that she felt like she WAS pressuring me.

So if we had paused at any point, I would have said no to the IUD, because I did not want one before the visit. But it was over kind of fast.

I left the office kind of in a haze, and then I broke down in tears at the bus stop. And now I'm traumatized and I don't want to go in again for my checkup in the summer. I'm thinking of filing a complaint.

Am I overreacting?

EDIT: Thank you all so much for the support and helping me to understand that this was much more serious than I first thought. It is much appreciated.

I have filed the complaint. I'll see how they respond and then I'll see if I'll take it further. I don't want to start a whole process, but I want the doctor to know she messed up.

Also, I checked the time of my bus ticket and the whole thing actually lasted closer to 30 minutes, which makes sense since there was the ultrasound as well. I guess that's a trauma response as well.

EDIT2: I did not sign anything. I don't know if you're supposed to do that here or not (I'm not in the US).

You can read in my story where I'm a little hazy because of the shock, but I am sure of that. I also never said yes to the IUD, I think she just assumed it was okay since I didn't say no either. She inserted it right after the the ultrasound. 

And it was not planned beforehand. Of that I'm sure we well, as I was just going to ask about birth control pills.

EDIT A MONTH LATER: I got an email from the senior physician of the department. It basically said "Sorry you felt like you were pressured. The doctor says you said yes to getting the IUD. There's nothing we can do about the pain anyway, bye." So it's basically my word against hers and I also had a problem with "You FELT like" so I responded, kindly. Just waiting on a response.
parent_comment: Are you shitting me? Seriously? Victim blaming? Procedures like this require WRITTEN consent in a lot of the world. They require sitting you down and explaining the ins and outs of it, the risks, how it works. They require so many things this woman did NOT get. Being pressured into consent is not consent. No proper medical professional would dream of pressuring their patient into something and backing them into a corner until they agree. That’s not consent.

title: Unpopular Opinion: I'm tired of hearing the whole "it's not your job to teach someone about XYZ"...
body:
I realize this will likely not be a popular post based on the number of times I see this phrase in the comments on this particular sub but I still wanted to share this, maybe controversial but ultimately, alternative view/thought process.

I hate willful ignorance probably more than anything, but being *"willfully ignorant of"* & just being *"ignorant of"* are different things. Some people grow up sheltered, privileged, unaware of the existence of prejudice or malice - They are ignorant in the sense that they don't yet know that another view, or experience, is different than their own. Willful ignorance however, is when someone knows those things but chooses to dismiss or ignore them altogether to remain close-minded. So when I see people say things like "It's not your job to teach your boyfriend about sexism" or "it's not your job to explain what privilege is to others" it bothers me because we were all ignorant of something, sometime in our life & if someone didn't teach us, we'd never know. I think it is our job, especially with those we're close with to at least try and help them understand something they may not be aware of. Now if the person does know & chooses to keep recognizing ONLY their experience, that's willful ignorance and it's not your job to "convince them" something merits consideration.

As an example, when I was around 18-19 I worked as a server/bartender and became good friends with this guy named Rocky. I should explain that I went to a small school (200 kids maybe) and it was almost completely white and I honestly had very little interaction with people from other races - which sucks btw - so there were a lot of things I didn't understand about the POC experience. Was I aware of racism? Yes, of course this is America but I didn't really understand the real life implications or experience of POC. Rocky was a black guy, and being friends with him was easy but I was constantly learning from him about his experience. One night we're working behind the bar together & this group comes in, they start ordering drinks but I also notice they keep calling Rocky, Tyrone. Now in my head I'm thinking they just can't see his name tag or maybe they misheard him, I'll correct them but when I do the guy just says "oh he your boyfriend or something?" I just said no, he's my friend & his name is Rocky but I realized this guy was *only* planning to respect Rocky if we were dating.

Later when the bar closed I asked Rocky what was up because I could see he was down. He explained how often that shit happened, where they'd use a "stereotypical black guy name" in a pejorative way unless a white person was around to give him "legitimacy". He told me about how these little things (micro-aggressions) had happened his whole life, how it affected him & his brothers. Rocky didn't have to share that with me, he could have taken the "it's not my job to explain racism to you" route but then I might never have understood micro-aggressions in the way I do now.

Yes I agree to some degree that it's every individuals responsibility to learn about how their experiences aren't shared by all, but I also think it's every one's job to help others who want to learn, understand them better. We don't all have the same experience and we don't all learn things at the same time so if it's not our job to help others understand, then whose job is it?

Really I guess this long rant is because I want to see more people sharing their experiences so we can understand them better and learn how to be better allies to each other. It would be amazing if people didn't need experiences like mine with Rocky to understand the weight of some things, but often it's just a lack of exposure and not willful ignorance.

**ETA: Due to the volume of messages attacking me, my husband and whatever minor semantics bothered people about this observation and request for more understanding I'm taking a break from the sub for a while. It's clear that while many are interested in using this forum for helping others understand women's perspectives, others are intent on using it to disparage others for simply not knowing something. I stand behind my statements.**
parent_comment:
First of all, thank you.  Putting your ideas out into a public forum can be an exercise in vulnerability and I appreciate you for putting yourself out there and being so thoughtful and thorough in both your original post and your responses.  From what I've read, your relationship with your husband sounds amazing and it never fails to make me happy to see examples of love flourishing!  

I count myself as one of the lucky ones because of the patience my wife has in sharing her experiences of living life as woman.  I will say with, absolute certainty, that I will never truly understand her life.  I just can't.  There is no way for me to experience life through a woman's perspective because I can't simply insert a filter composed of the accumulated exhaustion for daily injustices she experiences.  Even if I were to somehow able to relive all of that, it would still be seasoned through my own experiences!

It's unfortunate that men can't just understand, and I understand that it can get tiring to have to repeatedly hear things like "Imagine if it was your daughter.",  "Imagine if it was your wife.",  but without having some source of reference, I wouldn't have a clue and I think that's likely true for many men.  

Is it changing?  I think it is but I also think that work is arduous and slow.  It's fatiguing because taking the high road means you have to live it and then if you want change you have to teach it.  I appreciate this subreddit because it's a way to share experiences that I wouldn't normally be exposed to or understand (yet).  I appreciate it when someone will be patient with me and to help me understand because I know how heavy of an ask that is.  Sometimes the juice isn't worth the squeeze, but for everyone out there that shares their story, I very sincerely thank you and appreciate you because at there's at lease one person that you've made better for it (including your husband OP, there's at least two!).

Again, thanks for posting this.  I wouldn't know what I didn't know without people like you out there!

title: I went in to get an ultrasound and I left with an IUD without my explicit consent
body:
Long story short, I went to the gynecologic with the intention of getting myself checked out and asking about birth control. I left with an IUD in tears.

Long story:

At the start of the visit (that was about 20 minutes) the doctor told me that the pills I wanted wouldn't be a great fit because of my weight. I said okay, in my mind thinking that then I wouldn't get anything. I had never been on hormones and I was a little scared of the possible mood swings and such. This was also my second ever trip to the gynecologist and I was really nervous.

She asked me if I had considered a contraceptive implant or an IUD, but I said that I was scared of them both because I wouldn't be able to get them out myself.

She just said that I should think it over and that she'd be able to put the IUD in right now. I said that I was scared of the pain, so if it would hurt a lot to put it in, then I don't want it. I said that I had read horror stories about it. She didn't really say anything to that, and we started the examination.

In the end, there was nothing wrong, and then I'm not completely sure what happened next because of the shock and the pain. Suddenly she's opening the box and inserting the IUD and I kind of blacked out, I know I was screaming and it was absolute hell. The worst pain of my life. I didn't even take a painkiller before because I didn't know it was going to happen.

The nurse that was by my head (I guess there to keep me calm) was also kind of chuckling and commenting that my eyes were really wide and telling me to breathe. I guess trauma is funny. They did keep asking me if I was okay, but I was in shock and just said yes, I guess.

So the doctor didn't really explain anything about the IUD (I know how it works since I've researched it but she didn't know that) and didn't really get my consent to put it in either. I didn't explicitly say no, but I think she should have made sure? She also kept asking me if I felt like she was pressuring me, and I think that it was sign that she felt like she WAS pressuring me.

So if we had paused at any point, I would have said no to the IUD, because I did not want one before the visit. But it was over kind of fast.

I left the office kind of in a haze, and then I broke down in tears at the bus stop. And now I'm traumatized and I don't want to go in again for my checkup in the summer. I'm thinking of filing a complaint.

Am I overreacting?

EDIT: Thank you all so much for the support and helping me to understand that this was much more serious than I first thought. It is much appreciated.

I have filed the complaint. I'll see how they respond and then I'll see if I'll take it further. I don't want to start a whole process, but I want the doctor to know she messed up.

Also, I checked the time of my bus ticket and the whole thing actually lasted closer to 30 minutes, which makes sense since there was the ultrasound as well. I guess that's a trauma response as well.

EDIT2: I did not sign anything. I don't know if you're supposed to do that here or not (I'm not in the US).

You can read in my story where I'm a little hazy because of the shock, but I am sure of that. I also never said yes to the IUD, I think she just assumed it was okay since I didn't say no either. She inserted it right after the the ultrasound. 

And it was not planned beforehand. Of that I'm sure we well, as I was just going to ask about birth control pills.

EDIT A MONTH LATER: I got an email from the senior physician of the department. It basically said "Sorry you felt like you were pressured. The doctor says you said yes to getting the IUD. There's nothing we can do about the pain anyway, bye." So it's basically my word against hers and I also had a problem with "You FELT like" so I responded, kindly. Just waiting on a response.

First off, you’re not responsible for being assaulted. Freezing is a totally normal and common response to sexual assault.

Because we couldn’t undo it, and it was a shitty thing. 

And… it wasn’t my fault. Same as what happened to you wasn’t your fault. You can take accountability for what happened, but you don’t have to take responsibility for being assaulted.
