title: Unpopular Opinion: I'm tired of hearing the whole "it's not your job to teach someone about XYZ"...
body:
I realize this will likely not be a popular post based on the number of times I see this phrase in the comments on this particular sub but I still wanted to share this, maybe controversial but ultimately, alternative view/thought process.

I hate willful ignorance probably more than anything, but being *"willfully ignorant of"* & just being *"ignorant of"* are different things. Some people grow up sheltered, privileged, unaware of the existence of prejudice or malice - They are ignorant in the sense that they don't yet know that another view, or experience, is different than their own. Willful ignorance however, is when someone knows those things but chooses to dismiss or ignore them altogether to remain close-minded. So when I see people say things like "It's not your job to teach your boyfriend about sexism" or "it's not your job to explain what privilege is to others" it bothers me because we were all ignorant of something, sometime in our life & if someone didn't teach us, we'd never know. I think it is our job, especially with those we're close with to at least try and help them understand something they may not be aware of. Now if the person does know & chooses to keep recognizing ONLY their experience, that's willful ignorance and it's not your job to "convince them" something merits consideration.

As an example, when I was around 18-19 I worked as a server/bartender and became good friends with this guy named Rocky. I should explain that I went to a small school (200 kids maybe) and it was almost completely white and I honestly had very little interaction with people from other races - which sucks btw - so there were a lot of things I didn't understand about the POC experience. Was I aware of racism? Yes, of course this is America but I didn't really understand the real life implications or experience of POC. Rocky was a black guy, and being friends with him was easy but I was constantly learning from him about his experience. One night we're working behind the bar together & this group comes in, they start ordering drinks but I also notice they keep calling Rocky, Tyrone. Now in my head I'm thinking they just can't see his name tag or maybe they misheard him, I'll correct them but when I do the guy just says "oh he your boyfriend or something?" I just said no, he's my friend & his name is Rocky but I realized this guy was *only* planning to respect Rocky if we were dating.

Later when the bar closed I asked Rocky what was up because I could see he was down. He explained how often that shit happened, where they'd use a "stereotypical black guy name" in a pejorative way unless a white person was around to give him "legitimacy". He told me about how these little things (micro-aggressions) had happened his whole life, how it affected him & his brothers. Rocky didn't have to share that with me, he could have taken the "it's not my job to explain racism to you" route but then I might never have understood micro-aggressions in the way I do now.

Yes I agree to some degree that it's every individuals responsibility to learn about how their experiences aren't shared by all, but I also think it's every one's job to help others who want to learn, understand them better. We don't all have the same experience and we don't all learn things at the same time so if it's not our job to help others understand, then whose job is it?

Really I guess this long rant is because I want to see more people sharing their experiences so we can understand them better and learn how to be better allies to each other. It would be amazing if people didn't need experiences like mine with Rocky to understand the weight of some things, but often it's just a lack of exposure and not willful ignorance.

**ETA: Due to the volume of messages attacking me, my husband and whatever minor semantics bothered people about this observation and request for more understanding I'm taking a break from the sub for a while. It's clear that while many are interested in using this forum for helping others understand women's perspectives, others are intent on using it to disparage others for simply not knowing something. I stand behind my statements.**

Maybe some of these things will apply to your thought process or help.

You can be victimized and traumatized even if you feel like your experience wasn't as bad as other people's. Labeling yourself a victim or calling your experience assault does not detract from anyone else's experiences with assault. This isn't a zero sum game, and there's room for anyone who has been adversely affected by coercive/nonconsensual sexual experiences or experiences where they were misled or lied to about key information that affects consent. There is a broad spectrum of experiences that fall into SA, and they are ALL SA.

A lot of people don't like or aren't comfortable using the word victim, and that's ok. A lot of people prefer to call themselves survivors. A friend of mine said just the other day that she doesn't like either, as someone who has both experienced abuse and beaten cancer. In her words, "I think people can experience trauma without it defining them." If there's another word you want to use, or there is (now or ever) a healthy reason you don't want to use victim, then do what feels right for you. It sounds like right now at least, it isn't a healthy reason, but over time that can change, which is ok.

Which brings me to the last point: healing is a journey, and labeling your experiences and how you identify yourself in their context is a piece of that journey. Sometimes, you have to accept where you are, because if you focus on how far you still have to go, you'll minimize the progress you've already made. It's a good idea to pause and reflect periodically. It can help you decide how you want to move forward. You might also decide some of your survival tactics that got you to that point aren't helping anymore, and then you can let them go or repurpose them. That includes labels.

Sometimes, you don't necessarily have to do anything specific to build your comfort level with words, it just takes time. About 9 months ago, my now ex used the word "rape" to describe what he did. I think I have said that word out loud twice or maybe 3 times in reference to that experience, and every time has been quoting him. I've only said it to him, my therapist, and maybe a friend who was literally in the other room when it happened and who I'd already told what happened way before the label. I'm getting there. Talking about all of the things he put me through gets easier with distance and time, especially if I focus on how it affects me now.

Also, trauma-focused or trauma-informed therapy can be helpful for situations where you feel a cognitive dissonance like this. It can be a sign that you have learned thought processes or beliefs about yourself and your experiences that will fall apart if challenged the right way, "right" being dependent on the particular thought process or belief. I personally did cognitive processing therapy, and even though I "graduated" from that method about 5 years ago, I still use the tools I learned very often. I also still see a therapist regularly for traditional talk therapy.

I'm sorry that you had this happen to you. I'm sorry your ex couldn't respect your boundaries, and the first no. You have a right to control what happens to your body.

When you set boundaries and/or say no, that's it. Saying no doesn't mean he should keep asking, harassing, badgering, pleading, begging, or trying to guilt you until you say yes. Coercion is not consent.

I hope you will check out this [article](https://www.scarleteen.com/article/disability_quickies/quickies_sexual_consent_basics), and use it to empower yourself in standing up for your right to control what happens to your body. You have a right to say no. I hope in the future you cut anyone who can't respect not the first time, out of your life. If they can't respect your boundaries, then leave, that's it. No second chances, just leave. Anyone who disrespects you once, will try to do it again. And don't let them ever try to convince you that you are overreacting, it was a mistake, or they were drunk. Stand up for your right to control what happens to your body.

It's not your fault. It's not your fault because you had your boyfriend over. It's not your fault because he was in your room. It's not your fault because you might have done it had he had a condom. It's not your fault because he wouldn't respect your no and harassed you until you gave in. It's his. You said no, but he just cared about getting what he wanted, not what you wanted. He did this to you.

You deserve someone who cares about you and what you've been through. You deserve someone respects your boundaries and cares enough to make sure you want to and are enjoying all aspects of your relationship. You deserve so much more then what happened to you. And I hope you find everything you want in the future.

I'm sorry that this has, and is continuing to really affect you. If you aren't already in therapy, I hope you will give it some serious consideration. I feel like it could really help you. If you don't feel comfortable talking to someone in RL yet, I recommend checking out [Rainn.org](https://Rainn.org). There you can find lots of resources that may be of some help, including being able to talk to someone for free. They can just listen or, if you want, direct you in finding some help with how to handle things.

I hope you will look into getting some help. I pray that you can find the strength and support to keep moving forward, and that some day, with time, and some help, you can find some peace with what happened. Please stay strong, and be safe.

P.S. Please be very careful with anyone who tries to DM or chat you about this. There are creeps who will try to get you to tell them what happened for their own amusement. I recommend staying in the comments to avoid anybody hurting you further.

title: I went in to get an ultrasound and I left with an IUD without my explicit consent
body:
Long story short, I went to the gynecologic with the intention of getting myself checked out and asking about birth control. I left with an IUD in tears.

Long story:

At the start of the visit (that was about 20 minutes) the doctor told me that the pills I wanted wouldn't be a great fit because of my weight. I said okay, in my mind thinking that then I wouldn't get anything. I had never been on hormones and I was a little scared of the possible mood swings and such. This was also my second ever trip to the gynecologist and I was really nervous.

She asked me if I had considered a contraceptive implant or an IUD, but I said that I was scared of them both because I wouldn't be able to get them out myself.

She just said that I should think it over and that she'd be able to put the IUD in right now. I said that I was scared of the pain, so if it would hurt a lot to put it in, then I don't want it. I said that I had read horror stories about it. She didn't really say anything to that, and we started the examination.

In the end, there was nothing wrong, and then I'm not completely sure what happened next because of the shock and the pain. Suddenly she's opening the box and inserting the IUD and I kind of blacked out, I know I was screaming and it was absolute hell. The worst pain of my life. I didn't even take a painkiller before because I didn't know it was going to happen.

The nurse that was by my head (I guess there to keep me calm) was also kind of chuckling and commenting that my eyes were really wide and telling me to breathe. I guess trauma is funny. They did keep asking me if I was okay, but I was in shock and just said yes, I guess.

So the doctor didn't really explain anything about the IUD (I know how it works since I've researched it but she didn't know that) and didn't really get my consent to put it in either. I didn't explicitly say no, but I think she should have made sure? She also kept asking me if I felt like she was pressuring me, and I think that it was sign that she felt like she WAS pressuring me.

So if we had paused at any point, I would have said no to the IUD, because I did not want one before the visit. But it was over kind of fast.

I left the office kind of in a haze, and then I broke down in tears at the bus stop. And now I'm traumatized and I don't want to go in again for my checkup in the summer. I'm thinking of filing a complaint.

Am I overreacting?

EDIT: Thank you all so much for the support and helping me to understand that this was much more serious than I first thought. It is much appreciated.

I have filed the complaint. I'll see how they respond and then I'll see if I'll take it further. I don't want to start a whole process, but I want the doctor to know she messed up.

Also, I checked the time of my bus ticket and the whole thing actually lasted closer to 30 minutes, which makes sense since there was the ultrasound as well. I guess that's a trauma response as well.

EDIT2: I did not sign anything. I don't know if you're supposed to do that here or not (I'm not in the US).

You can read in my story where I'm a little hazy because of the shock, but I am sure of that. I also never said yes to the IUD, I think she just assumed it was okay since I didn't say no either. She inserted it right after the the ultrasound. 

And it was not planned beforehand. Of that I'm sure we well, as I was just going to ask about birth control pills.

EDIT A MONTH LATER: I got an email from the senior physician of the department. It basically said "Sorry you felt like you were pressured. The doctor says you said yes to getting the IUD. There's nothing we can do about the pain anyway, bye." So it's basically my word against hers and I also had a problem with "You FELT like" so I responded, kindly. Just waiting on a response.
parent_comment: Hell to the fucking no. I’m from Finland and this kind of thing should absolutely not happen. The doctor did not have your clear consent as you never said a clear ”yes” to the IUD. Please check www.valvira.fi and www.stm.fi (Sosiaali- ja terveysministeriö) as they are the official government bodies overseeing the health care workers in Finland.

body:

I think that for the sake of this story and because I need to vent- I need to add some background.
Recently my life has became very difficult as I’ve been struggling a lot with problems with my mental health- which were made a lot more difficult when I broke up with my boyfriend almost exactly a month ago.

On Halloween, c dressed as hugh heffner and I was a playbunny. our friend had a big house party; where everyone at the party was extremely drunk and whatever else- especially me and C. We had an inside joke between us that because November was fast approaching- we should both look for people at the party to hook up with. Neither of us achieved this goal in the end.
I was at the level of drunk where I was tired, and everyone was setting up their beds and settling down. Me and c were hugging on the sofa- and eventually we accidentally ended up falling sleep hugging into each-other. I remember feeling a large burst of comfort and love when I woke up. Later on in the night, I’m going to say around 5 or 6am, I woke up to the feeling of my ass being touched and groped and squeezed. All it took for this to not happen would’ve been me turning around at the start and telling him not to or batting his hand away- but there was two other people sleeping in the same room and in my head I believed that this would have somehow caused a scene and embarrassed him. My decision making, looking back, could have been influenced by any drugs and alcohol I had taken. But I’m convinced that when this occurred I was sober. 
Eventually, I woke up to go to the bathroom because I needed to pee, but I stayed for a long time in the bathroom because I couldn’t stop shaking. I didn’t cry- I just shook. I noticed that my costume was doused in period blood, and I remember feeling frustrated that this occurrence had ruined my costume.

Eventually he returned as if nothing had happened and I gave him the couch as I slept on the floor.
The next day, he left quite early and I spent the rest of it talking to other friends and travelling home. When I got back I slept for the entire day. 
Since then I’ve seen him a number of times. I saw him that morning, and we go to the same college and even travel on the bus together to go. We pretended like nothing had happened and I even joked with him, but he noticed that something was ‘off’ with me. 
This is until last night, where he messages me and asks me if something is going on. He tells me he knows full well what was going on, and he knows he sexually assaulted me. He tells me the details incase I wasn’t fully aware myself; which in hindsight actually gave me clarification. I thought he had at one point had sex with me or attempted to, but he assures me that he hadn’t. We have a long talk through text and concluded that the future will have what it has, but we both definitely for the time being need to have space from each-other. I tell him that he doesn’t need to worry about this coming back to him and that I’m not going to tell anyone about this- and if I did it wouldn’t be by name. I don’t want his life to be ruined- I love him too much. 
Without his presence that was always there before, I’ve been feeling empty. Our friendship was to the extent we would call or talk every night, and he would even stay at my house occasionally. 
I can’t help but think constantly that If I had just turned around and told him no- everything would be okay. My entire lifestyle has to change because of this. Our group of friends that we’ve had for up to five years is certainly going to be different. We go to the gym together, tell each other everything about each other and are both each others biggest supporters. I have ruined it.
I’ve only told one of my friends about this incident who tells me that my thinking about being at fault is flawed and it was definitely sexual assault. Even c spent a lot of our conversation assuring me that I was assaulted- but I’m still not convinced.
I think that at the time, because I didn’t do anything and even made it easier for him to do what he did- I had actually wanted it and didn’t realise it. Otherwise I would’ve made a bigger effort to stop him.
I think it’s also useful to mention that something me and C bonded over is that we both have certain kinks, and a part of me is telling me that my fetish for this had fuelled my decision making in this instant; but it still felt disgusting and violating- not like when I would practice this sort of kink with previous partners.

As far as I know however, that wasn’t involved with anything that wasn’t consensual. I’ve thrown my costume in the trash. All I wish is that things could have been like they were before

title: Unpopular Opinion: I'm tired of hearing the whole "it's not your job to teach someone about XYZ"...
body:
I realize this will likely not be a popular post based on the number of times I see this phrase in the comments on this particular sub but I still wanted to share this, maybe controversial but ultimately, alternative view/thought process.

I hate willful ignorance probably more than anything, but being *"willfully ignorant of"* & just being *"ignorant of"* are different things. Some people grow up sheltered, privileged, unaware of the existence of prejudice or malice - They are ignorant in the sense that they don't yet know that another view, or experience, is different than their own. Willful ignorance however, is when someone knows those things but chooses to dismiss or ignore them altogether to remain close-minded. So when I see people say things like "It's not your job to teach your boyfriend about sexism" or "it's not your job to explain what privilege is to others" it bothers me because we were all ignorant of something, sometime in our life & if someone didn't teach us, we'd never know. I think it is our job, especially with those we're close with to at least try and help them understand something they may not be aware of. Now if the person does know & chooses to keep recognizing ONLY their experience, that's willful ignorance and it's not your job to "convince them" something merits consideration.

As an example, when I was around 18-19 I worked as a server/bartender and became good friends with this guy named Rocky. I should explain that I went to a small school (200 kids maybe) and it was almost completely white and I honestly had very little interaction with people from other races - which sucks btw - so there were a lot of things I didn't understand about the POC experience. Was I aware of racism? Yes, of course this is America but I didn't really understand the real life implications or experience of POC. Rocky was a black guy, and being friends with him was easy but I was constantly learning from him about his experience. One night we're working behind the bar together & this group comes in, they start ordering drinks but I also notice they keep calling Rocky, Tyrone. Now in my head I'm thinking they just can't see his name tag or maybe they misheard him, I'll correct them but when I do the guy just says "oh he your boyfriend or something?" I just said no, he's my friend & his name is Rocky but I realized this guy was *only* planning to respect Rocky if we were dating.

Later when the bar closed I asked Rocky what was up because I could see he was down. He explained how often that shit happened, where they'd use a "stereotypical black guy name" in a pejorative way unless a white person was around to give him "legitimacy". He told me about how these little things (micro-aggressions) had happened his whole life, how it affected him & his brothers. Rocky didn't have to share that with me, he could have taken the "it's not my job to explain racism to you" route but then I might never have understood micro-aggressions in the way I do now.

Yes I agree to some degree that it's every individuals responsibility to learn about how their experiences aren't shared by all, but I also think it's every one's job to help others who want to learn, understand them better. We don't all have the same experience and we don't all learn things at the same time so if it's not our job to help others understand, then whose job is it?

Really I guess this long rant is because I want to see more people sharing their experiences so we can understand them better and learn how to be better allies to each other. It would be amazing if people didn't need experiences like mine with Rocky to understand the weight of some things, but often it's just a lack of exposure and not willful ignorance.

**ETA: Due to the volume of messages attacking me, my husband and whatever minor semantics bothered people about this observation and request for more understanding I'm taking a break from the sub for a while. It's clear that while many are interested in using this forum for helping others understand women's perspectives, others are intent on using it to disparage others for simply not knowing something. I stand behind my statements.**

Family and close friends deserve the benefit of the doubt, that they're not trying to be harmful. Obviously, if they don't bother to try and understand and are toxic then that's a whole other story.

title: Midwife vs OBGYN Doctor for childbirth - anecdotal review
body:
For my first baby, I just went to the maternity clinic at the hospital that my family doctor referred me to… I didn’t really have a preference or did any research so I just went along with it. It was a rotating service for doctors that work at the hospital and the care was clinical and minimal - It was typically 45 minutes in the waiting room, 5-10 minute appointment, no bedside manner or asking about me, I was just an incubator. I always felt really nervous to ask questions and just did whatever they told me to. 

For my second, I knew early on I wanted to try a different approach and went with a midwife. I’m only 28 weeks along but cannot praise this approach enough. They take their time and make it personal, it’s about me and my experience, they ask me multiple times throughout the appointment if I have any questions, they let me know my options with different tests and what the results mean in a tangible way, there’s always samples of vitamins/supplements/formula/diapers in the office, they let me know that my needs came first… it just is a better overall experience. 

I also want to stress that my first pregnancy had no complications and I had a fairly ‘easy’ natural childbirth so my family doctor said midwife would be a good choice. Both of my sisters had issues and c-section so they chose to stick with an ob. 

I’m in Canada so there was no extra cost either way, midwives have hospital privileges and I’ll still be giving birth at the hospital. They also provide care to me and baby from 8weeks preg-6 weeks postpartum.
parent_comment: There's a third option which is to have a family medicine obstetrical group manage your pregnancy. They are MDs so they have a better approach to non specific complaints that may or not be related to your pregnancy but they will also provide with the time and attention of a midwife. Plus after birth you already have a family doctor set up for yourself and your baby or any future babies.

title: Boundaries invaded
body:

I backed away from surprise, but I hit my back on the door hinge (which hurt a lot). I told he not to do that again, which he said okay. Later I talked to him about boundaries, and when I asked him about the situation he said he didn't remember (he was high, long story). He's a very touchy person and i dont really like being touched (platonic gestures specifically) unless there's consent and/or I'm initiating it. He clearly didn't mean to do it from what I can tell, and it was a miscommunication, but I just can't stop thinking about it and it's anxiety inducing cause he's in two of my classes. I'm gonna talk to my therapist about it today, but I don't know how to get it out of my head.

He also suffers from sexual assault trauma. I've discussed it with my friends who knew him before and they said he was genuinely touchy and also just a shitty person when it came to boundaries.

Is this sexual assault? Even if it's not sexual, then what is it?

Edit: i added a trigger warning, and more info.
parent_comment: It is.  I’m sorry you’re going through this.  It’s so hard when someone violates our autonomy like that, and to get hurt at the same time because of his bad behavior just adds salt to the wound.   I would avoid this person as best you can.  I know it can be nice having friends who “get” you, and it can be tempting to put more trust in people who share certain qualities with us, because we think they empathize better what it’s like to be treated unfairly.  But that’s not always the case.  It’s a rainbow of all types, and there will be bad apples like anywhere.  Keep looking, you’ll find more good ones 💕

title: I was raped but I don’t know what to feel. I’m confused
body:
Please read it all because I need help and advice
⚠️TW: SEXUAL ASSAULT AND SELF HARM⚠️ 

A few weeks ago I (19f) was raped by a guy I don’t know at a party. I was really drunk and didn’t consent to it happening but all I remember is being in the room and I was drugged. I remember him being on top of me and from then, I black out and I don’t remember anything that happened. He admitted to the police to having “consented sex” with me but I was unconscious and I didn’t consent so that’s just wild. But ever since it happened I’ve just felt so weird because I don’t remember anything so I don’t know if I’m supposed to be getting support or if I’m an actual victim or anything. But I’ll list all the things that have been happening to me so far since it’s happened.

Just to preface, I have autism and a semi BPD (borderline) diagnosis. My doctors have also spoken about me having an anxiety disorder.

•	⁠I’m finding it harder to sleep, so sometimes I won’t sleep for days at a time because I’m scared to sleep as when I do, I end up having night terrors or getting flashbacks. This leaves me waking up sweaty, with a racing heart, quick breathing, stressed and scared and often leads to a panic attack. I’ve had panic attacks before so this isn’t new but they do last a bit longer and during my panic attacks I feel like I can’t breathe and I pull at my hair.
•	⁠I can’t concentrate nor do I have the motivation to do anything anymore. I’m in university so I need to attend my lectures but I haven’t been in 2 going on to 3 weeks now and I’m very behind but I just can’t do my work. Nothing is registering in my brain and I feel stupid and like a failure because I’m so behind on everything.
•	⁠I’m losing motivation when it comes to my personal health and hygiene. I will lay in bed all day in the dark deep in thought or zoned out and I don’t brush my teeth or shower or eat any food. I can go 2-3 days without doing any of these but then I start feeling sick and like I’m going to pass out so I force myself to get in the shower and eat something. Even cooking and buying groceries is such a pain. I don’t want to do it anymore.
•	⁠Some days I’ll just feel numb and empty and like I’m living life on autopilot, almost like a robot and these days seem to be easier because I don’t feel anything. I’ll just feel disconnected from reality and my days feel like they’re blurring together. Other days I’m angry at everything, at my friends, at myself, at my situation and at my life. I just get angry and start crying and hitting myself in the head and want to self harm (cutting).
•	⁠Sometimes I feel like I can’t control my mind or my emotions I feel like I’m being taken over and I’ll just get so mad or so upset and start crying and having a breakdown, which less than often leads to a panic attack and sometimes leads to self harm where I’ll usually cut myself or hit/ punch myself in the head and throw things and after I’ll feel more depressed and annoyed with myself and regret what I did after.
•	⁠Nothing is fun anymore. I’ve been depressed since before I was a teenager and I could have my friends or hobbies as an escape but now I don’t want to talk to my friends, I don’t want to do my art or play my instrument or watch my shows or do anything. I wish I could disappear and be alone with a clear mind.
•	⁠I smoke weed and have for a few years as it helps me sleep at night and block/ slow down unwanted thoughts in my mind, but since I’ve been put on Sertraline/ Zoloft it’s made me really paranoid so I’ve had to quit smoking. But now I’m having more restless nights and I feel on edge and worried all the time and I just want to run far away.
•	⁠I feel like I don’t know what I’m doing with myself sometimes, almost unpredictable. A few nights ago, around 1am I was really down in the dumps and I just wanted to feel alive so I took a couple bumps of Ketamine and went on a bike ride in -3° weather. My fingers started going numb so I stopped to smoke some weed even though I was supposed to quit and smoked it but then I realised I didn’t know where I was since I started cycling randomly and I started panicking, broke down crying and just got an uber home.
•	⁠When I speak to someone or I’m in my lecture or on the bus I often zone out and forget what’s being said or what’s going on around me and I have to focus extra hard. I feel out of it and like I’m not processing what’s going on around me.
•	⁠I tried to take my own life about a week after it happened and I got sent to the psych ward but I was released after two days. Then they gave me antidepressants and I’ve been taking them for a week.
•	⁠I started self harming again after being clean for months and I don’t know why, maybe I just wanted to feel something again? I keep getting thoughts of wanting to self harm and end my life cause I feel like there’s no point of anything anymore and nothing even matters.
•	⁠When I try opening up to my friend they keep being strange and annoying. For example, people who know about the situation will ask them how I’m doing if I’m not around since we live near, and they will come to me and tell me that people asked about me and they will be like “What about me?! Why are they not asking how I’m doing?!” and it annoys me and throws me off cause it’s not really about you right now you know. Maybe I’m being selfish. When I express how I’m feeling, be this depressed or like I don’t wanna be here anymore, they will start complaining about things in their life and saying how the fact that I’m depressed is making them depressed and if I did anything to myself they wouldn’t be able to live and then I’d have to comfort them and it’s just kind of strange, like it’s a depression olympics or something. I try not to think about it too deeply cause they’re my friend but it annoys the hell out of me and so I don’t like opening up to them anymore cause it’s always weird. Not to say they can’t open up to me, they always can but they only do it when I do it so that’s why I feel like it’s weird.

I just feel alone because I can’t tell anyone how I’m feeling. I don’t have any friends or family who I’m close enough to open up to, and the only people that I think I can I don’t feel comfortable telling them all this cause what can they do for me? I guess this was a huge rant and stuff I needed to get off my chest and see if people can help me with what’s going on in my mind and any advice would be helpful. I’ve tried talking therapy in the past but that was awful I’ll never do that again so anything else would be appreciated.
parent_comment: Girl I am so proud of how hard you are trying to cope <3 , I think doing meditation , yoga or just being very spiritual really helps <3

title: Unpopular Opinion: I'm tired of hearing the whole "it's not your job to teach someone about XYZ"...

So when I see people say things like "It's not your job to teach your boyfriend about sexism" or "it's not your job to explain what privilege is to others" it bothers me because we were all ignorant of something, sometime in our life & if someone didn't teach us, we'd never know. I think it is our job, especially with those we're close with to at least try and help them understand something they may not be aware of. Now if the person does know & chooses to keep recognizing ONLY their experience, that's willful ignorance and it's not your job to "convince them" something merits consideration.

As an example, when I was around 18-19 I worked as a server/bartender and became good friends with this guy named Rocky. I should explain that I went to a small school (200 kids maybe) and it was almost completely white and I honestly had very little interaction with people from other races - which sucks btw - so there were a lot of things I didn't understand about the POC experience. Now in my head I'm thinking they just can't see his name tag or maybe they misheard him, I'll correct them but when I do the guy just says "oh he your boyfriend or something?" Some people are just closed minded and while they seem to genuinely want to understand they can never bring themselves to accept any answers they find or are given. I should explain that I went to a small school (200 kids maybe) and it was almost completely white and I honestly had very little interaction with people from other races - which sucks btw - so there were a lot of things I didn't understand about the POC experience. Was I aware of racism? Yes, of course this is America but I didn't really understand the real life implications or experience of POC. Rocky was a black guy, and being friends with him was easy but I was constantly learning from him about his experience. One night we're working behind the bar together & this group comes in, they start ordering drinks but I also notice they keep calling Rocky, Tyrone. Now in my head I'm thinking they just can't see his name tag or maybe they misheard him, I'll correct them but when I do the guy just says "oh he your boyfriend or something?" I just said no, he's my friend & his name is Rocky but I realized this guy was *only* planning to respect Rocky if we were dating.

Later when the bar closed I asked Rocky what was up because I could see he was down. He explained how often that shit happened, where they'd use a "stereotypical black guy name" in a pejorative way unless a white person was around to give him "legitimacy". He told me about how these little things (micro-aggressions) had happened his whole life, how it affected him & his brothers. Rocky didn't have to share that with me, he could have taken the "it's not my job to explain racism to you" route but then I might never have understood micro-aggressions in the way I do now.

Yes I agree to some degree that it's every individuals responsibility to learn about how their experiences aren't shared by all, but I also think it's every one's job to help others who want to learn, understand them better. We don't all have the same experience and we don't all learn things at the same time so if it's not our job to help others understand, then whose job is it?

Really I guess this long rant is because I want to see more people sharing their experiences so we can understand them better and learn how to be better allies to each other. It would be amazing if people didn't need experiences like mine with Rocky to understand the weight of some things, but often it's just a lack of exposure and not willful ignorance.

**ETA: Due to the volume of messages attacking me, my husband and whatever minor semantics bothered people about this observation and request for more understanding I'm taking a break from the sub for a while. It's clear that while many are interested in using this forum for helping others understand women's perspectives, others are intent on using it to disparage others for simply not knowing something. I stand behind my statements.**
parent_comment:
As one of those guys who is here to learn I've taken the stance of "of course it's not your job or responsibility, but I really appreciate it when it happens so I can be a better person and better advocate"

Some people aren't good at teaching.  Some people are having a bad day and just don't have the patience to deal with an idiot like me.  A lot of women have been manipulated so many times they've lost trust in strangers wanting to learn and think it's some kind of time trap/suck.  All of that is valid.  All of that is real.

I guess I just believe in doing my best until I know better.  Sometimes there will be opportunities I don't know about or can't capitalize on to know better, it happens and there's nothing for it.  As one nerd-dom has pointed out "It is possible to commit no mistakes and still lose. That is not a weakness. That is life."

title: With an ex boyfriend...?
body:
I have a lot on my mind, and I wanted to ask whether this was sexual assault. Sorry if it's a long read...

\-

  

**August 2018.** 

My boyfriend had come to visit for a few days as it was the yearly carnival, and I wanted him to come. As usual, he booked a hotel in the city centre, and I stayed over with him. It was the Monday, which was parade day! I was very excited for this. We were in the hotel room when we got frisky, though I was conscious of the time and didn’t truly want to have sex to begin with.

To add, at the time, we were experimenting with safe words for the fun of it. “My Melody” was our agreed safe word. **My Melody**. Those were the words that I stated when we were having sex. Perhaps he thought I was joking the first time; I was somewhat laughing after all. **My Melody**. *Oh?* *You continue?* I wanted to go to the parade. **My Melody**. *You don’t stop*. Well, three’s the limit. I shut down and let him have his fun.

I was silent from the moment he climaxed. We travelled to the carnival in silence. 

**What was it?**

I ended up walking away from him after a bit of a spat, and thanks to the crowds, it took about 15 minutes for him and me to find each other. He was seething. He pulled me aside and demanded to know what was wrong.

“I asked you to stop multiple times, but you didn’t!”

“Is that it? Or is there something else?” He asked incredulously. 

“That was it…”

“Good, because I was thinking that there was something else wrong too!” He was very angry.

**What was it?**

He was angry at the time, for there was always more than one thing I was upset about, apparently. I didn’t think it was my fault for having a train wreck of a life. Our relationship was also a bit turbulent at the time and issues were creeping up. Did he apologise? No. I was shocked about how dismissive he was about my concerns.

Instead he spoke of his frustrations to me a little later and said words which should have hurt my feelings. But I was numbed. I had more pressing concerns. We ended up leaving the carnival early, and I didn’t get to see the parade. 

If he was so angry though about something else, perhaps I was overreacting. He paid no heed to the event until I brought it up a while later and received a proper apology. It didn’t happen again.

**What was it?** 

I just don’t know. I shoved it to the back of my mind because I couldn’t cope with the feelings of… betrayal? Or perhaps I was just being dramatic… he was my boyfriend after all. It should not be a big deal. Right? He said he thought I was joking, I think it was mainly to do with how I sounded? So, in the end I wrote it off as miscommunication, but I did point out I said it three times… it was too overwhelming to think about so I "forgot" about it for a few months until another event (may make another post about the other event another time) made the memories come back, then things got worse and I forgot again until a few months ago when... I was in deep despair.

The relationship went downhill from there for a while. Let’s just say that the only reason why things improved was because my father ended up dying in early 2019 and I had no one else to lean on but him. I want to talk about ask about another event, but I think I’ll save that for another post.

So yeah, was this sexual assault, or just me overreacting and probably just looking for an excuse to have the spotlight on me? If it's the latter please let me know so I know what to do... thank you... from one tortured soul for a variety of reasons, 

NotCinny :')

What happened is not your fault at all, the blame lies completely on him and the fact he shrugged it off as "is that it" was probably either because he's done it before or because he wanted to plant the doubt in your mind that it wasn't bad so he could get away with it. title: Is it normal to not be phased by what happened to you?
body:

We might've spoken but 3-4 times before he invited me over to his place to hang out. Being dumb and attention starved I agreed as I figured I never get invited over by anyone and despite being suspicious and uncomfortable by the idea I figured that's how friends are made and I shouldn't be shy. When I got there he locked the room which I figured was fair since he has dormmates he only shares a bathroom and a hallway with. But he was immediately even more flirty and touchy than usual. I tried to ignore it and avoid it, but it escalated very quickly. He cuddled up to me, caressed me, played with my hands despite me being clearly uncomfortable and telling him so. He ended up kissing me multiple times by force and mocked the way I pushed him away and asked him to stop as if it was cute. He mentioned he'd "go further, but he was afraid his dormmates would hear. plus I probably wouldn't let him". 

  
I left not too long afterwards, he has apologized multiple times since then. We saw each other again a couple of times and he still has it in his head that we're dating and it's just taking me time to warm up to him or whatever. He still asks me to come over and that he "won't do stupid shit this time". I won't comply.

  
I'm surprised what happened didn't affect me as much as I imagined it should. I always thought people who go through these things end up scarred, nightmare-ridden and traumatized, but I've pretty much felt the same. It's hard to even recall that night, so maybe I just suppressed everything. I don't think about it at all, not unintentionally anyway. Every so often I think about it on purpose because I feel "I'm supposed to be thinking about this", but it barely gets a reaction out of me. I can't help, but feel like maybe it's because it wasn't that bad and I'm overreacting. I even felt bad for not liking the guy back. If I had liked him back I probably would've loved what happened and we'd be a couple right now which would've been nice given I've been healing from a heartbreak from 7 months ago. The one time somebody likes me, I don't like them back. What a waste.

  
I just don't know how to feel. Is it normal to not be phased by these things sometimes? Does it just take time for the realization to kick in? Was what happened really just not that bad? I mean I'm glad I feel alright, I'm just,, lost in a way? I feel guilty for not feeling worse, like I'm offending and belittling people who've gone through the same and felt worse.
parent_comment:
Well, firstly let’s digest this part 

>If I had liked him back, I probably would’ve loved what happened 

And let’s reword it

>If I had consented, I would’ve enjoyed it 

Of course you would’ve enjoyed it, because you would’ve been consenting! But what happened wasn’t consensual. He assaulted you. 

This can apply to literally any scenario. 

“Well if he didn’t assault me and allowed me to consent and I liked him and things felt safe and he respected my boundaries and was a good person and had good communication and..and..(etc)..then I would’ve liked it!”

If we need to change a person and situation entirely to become “okay” with it, it wasn’t a good situation. He wasn’t a good person.

You pushed him off, didn’t consent, etc and he still tried to pressure you and I believe the only reason he didn’t go further is because of his roommates. He was scared you’d scream or make a fuss and expose his behavior. 

You don’t NEED to feel a huge reaction. Sometimes being numb is part of trauma but also it could just..not be that damaging for you emotionally. Not everyone reacts to SA the same. BUT, to clarify, just because you weren’t drugged or brutally raped or something doesn’t mean this wasn’t SA. It very much was. 

Don’t force yourself to feel things if you don’t. But definitely do not continue talking to him. He WILL actually rape you if you do. Again, the only thing stopping him was the fear of being caught.


**edit** he literally said he would’ve gone further but he was worried about his roommates. Meaning he saw you pushing him off, saying no, etc and STILL would’ve went further and WANTED TO. This is a man who will rape you if given the opportunity. Cut him off.

He needed 9 points to be met for this to be consensual. He failed on each and every one. This was sexual assault no matter how you look at it.

title: Unpopular Opinion: I'm tired of hearing the whole "it's not your job to teach someone about XYZ"...
body:
I realize this will likely not be a popular post based on the number of times I see this phrase in the comments on this particular sub but I still wanted to share this, maybe controversial but ultimately, alternative view/thought process.

I hate willful ignorance probably more than anything, but being *"willfully ignorant of"* & just being *"ignorant of"* are different things. Some people grow up sheltered, privileged, unaware of the existence of prejudice or malice - They are ignorant in the sense that they don't yet know that another view, or experience, is different than their own. Willful ignorance however, is when someone knows those things but chooses to dismiss or ignore them altogether to remain close-minded. So when I see people say things like "It's not your job to teach your boyfriend about sexism" or "it's not your job to explain what privilege is to others" it bothers me because we were all ignorant of something, sometime in our life & if someone didn't teach us, we'd never know. I think it is our job, especially with those we're close with to at least try and help them understand something they may not be aware of. Now if the person does know & chooses to keep recognizing ONLY their experience, that's willful ignorance and it's not your job to "convince them" something merits consideration.

As an example, when I was around 18-19 I worked as a server/bartender and became good friends with this guy named Rocky. I should explain that I went to a small school (200 kids maybe) and it was almost completely white and I honestly had very little interaction with people from other races - which sucks btw - so there were a lot of things I didn't understand about the POC experience. Was I aware of racism? Yes, of course this is America but I didn't really understand the real life implications or experience of POC. Rocky was a black guy, and being friends with him was easy but I was constantly learning from him about his experience. One night we're working behind the bar together & this group comes in, they start ordering drinks but I also notice they keep calling Rocky, Tyrone. Now in my head I'm thinking they just can't see his name tag or maybe they misheard him, I'll correct them but when I do the guy just says "oh he your boyfriend or something?" I just said no, he's my friend & his name is Rocky but I realized this guy was *only* planning to respect Rocky if we were dating.

Later when the bar closed I asked Rocky what was up because I could see he was down. He explained how often that shit happened, where they'd use a "stereotypical black guy name" in a pejorative way unless a white person was around to give him "legitimacy". He told me about how these little things (micro-aggressions) had happened his whole life, how it affected him & his brothers. Rocky didn't have to share that with me, he could have taken the "it's not my job to explain racism to you" route but then I might never have understood micro-aggressions in the way I do now.

Yes I agree to some degree that it's every individuals responsibility to learn about how their experiences aren't shared by all, but I also think it's every one's job to help others who want to learn, understand them better. We don't all have the same experience and we don't all learn things at the same time so if it's not our job to help others understand, then whose job is it?

Really I guess this long rant is because I want to see more people sharing their experiences so we can understand them better and learn how to be better allies to each other. It would be amazing if people didn't need experiences like mine with Rocky to understand the weight of some things, but often it's just a lack of exposure and not willful ignorance.

**ETA: Due to the volume of messages attacking me, my husband and whatever minor semantics bothered people about this observation and request for more understanding I'm taking a break from the sub for a while. It's clear that while many are interested in using this forum for helping others understand women's perspectives, others are intent on using it to disparage others for simply not knowing something. I stand behind my statements.**
parent_comment:
The reason your opinion is unpopular is because you're expecting a marginalized person to explain their life when if you truly wanted to understand you could Google and find out for yourself. You can Google most any topic and find tons of information, including groups where members go and share experiences. You can lurk there just reading and learning about others without making someone else do the work for them. Like men do here. 

Example: I had a male friend who I used to think was a really good guy. But after a while I noticed he had some misogynistic views. Like making fun of me when I was on my period. Like not standing up for women who were being ogled by men. I would explain why those things were harmful and where he could find out how sexism affects women. Know what his response was? Oh I'll just wait until I see you and you can show me. I think the problem most of us have is the other persons entitlement to our time. As women we are socially conditioned to be kind, patient, empathic and as a result we do most of the emotional labor. It isn't my job to explain to a grown ass man why certain things aren't acceptable. I wouldn't mind having discussions with someone who had done their own research and wanted to hear personal experiences but I'm not doing the job of educating a fully functioning adult with resources who is too close-minded or lazy to do their own work.

title: apart from him trying to touch me I did everything
body:
I realize this will likely not be a popular post based on the number of times I see this phrase in the comments on this particular sub but I still wanted to share this, maybe controversial but ultimately, alternative view/thought process.

I hate willful ignorance probably more than anything, but being *"willfully ignorant of"* & just being *"ignorant of"* are different things. Some people grow up sheltered, privileged, unaware of the existence of prejudice or malice - They are ignorant in the sense that they don't yet know that another view, or experience, is different than their own. Willful ignorance however, is when someone knows those things but chooses to dismiss or ignore them altogether to remain close-minded. So when I see people say things like "It's not your job to teach your boyfriend about sexism" or "it's not your job to explain what privilege is to others" it bothers me because we were all ignorant of something, sometime in our life & if someone didn't teach us, we'd never know. I think it is our job, especially with those we're close with to at least try and help them understand something they may not be aware of. Now if the person does know & chooses to keep recognizing ONLY their experience, that's willful ignorance and it's not your job to "convince them" something merits consideration.

As an example, when I was around 18-19 I worked as a server/bartender and became good friends with this guy named Rocky. I should explain that I went to a small school (200 kids maybe) and it was almost completely white and I honestly had very little interaction with people from other races - which sucks btw - so there were a lot of things I didn't understand about the POC experience. Was I aware of racism? Yes, of course this is America but I didn't really understand the real life implications or experience of POC. Rocky was a black guy, and being friends with him was easy but I was constantly learning from him about his experience. One night we're working behind the bar together & this group comes in, they start ordering drinks but I also notice they keep calling Rocky, Tyrone. Now in my head I'm thinking they just can't see his name tag or maybe they misheard him, I'll correct them but when I do the guy just says "oh he your boyfriend or something?" I just said no, he's my friend & his name is Rocky but I realized this guy was *only* planning to respect Rocky if we were dating.

Later when the bar closed I asked Rocky what was up because I could see he was down. He explained how often that shit happened, where they'd use a "stereotypical black guy name" in a pejorative way unless a white person was around to give him "legitimacy". He told me about how these little things (micro-aggressions) had happened his whole life, how it affected him & his brothers. Rocky didn't have to share that with me, he could have taken the "it's not my job to explain racism to you" route but then I might never have understood micro-aggressions in the way I do now.

Yes I agree to some degree that it's every individuals responsibility to learn about how their experiences aren't shared by all, but I also think it's every one's job to help others who want to learn, understand them better. We don't all have the same experience and we don't all learn things at the same time so if it's not our job to help others understand, then whose job is it?

Really I guess this long rant is because I want to see more people sharing their experiences so we can understand them better and learn how to be better allies to each other. It would be amazing if people didn't need experiences like mine with Rocky to understand the weight of some things, but often it's just a lack of exposure and not willful ignorance.

**ETA: Due to the volume of messages attacking me, my husband and whatever minor semantics bothered people about this observation and request for more understanding I'm taking a break from the sub for a while. It's clear that while many are interested in using this forum for helping others understand women's perspectives, others are intent on using it to disparage others for simply not knowing something. I stand behind my statements.**
parent_comment:
I'm not asking you to educate me. I'm saying, while it certainly IS NOT your JOB to educate others, if you are going to engage with others, it's beneficial to society to educate them when they are undereducated.

You certainly don't have to do anything. It's something people can do to make the world a better place. I believe the OP was trying to make the case that simply saying "not my job" doesn't advance society. Is it likely to achieve the desired result? Or is it just a lazy way of accepting the ignorance of others?

Again, it's not your job. That much is true. But it also represents giving up. And if you are at the end of your rope, that's ok.

Okay first things first, here's the basics of consent. 

There is something called the FRIES acronym. It states that unless all of these conditions are met, sex or sexual activity is not sex, it is rape or assult. Someone used it to explain to me why what happened to me was rape. Since I've been in this sub I use this alot to explain to people why what happened to them wasn't okay.

So for consent to be valid it must meet the following conditions. 

FRIES stands for -

F - Freely given. If you have to pester someone for consent, ask them over and over again, tell them that if they loved you they would sleep with you, then consent is not freely given, you manipulated them into giving it.
R - Reversable. If you say yes, but then by the time you've made it to the bedroom you change your mind, then you can withdraw that consent. If you are having sex, and you change your mind, the minute you say no, or stop, consent has been withdrawn. If he forces you after that or doesn't stop immediately, then that is rape.
I - Informed. Consent must be informed consent. That means that you should know all of the potential risks and benefits of that activity. If you do not know that by having sex with someone you could catch an STD that they know they have, then that was not informed consent.
E - Enthusiastic. There should be absolutely no questioning wether you want to take part in sexual activity. If you do not say, 'Oh! Yes please, that would be lovely!' but instead you are saying 'Urgh. Go on then.'that is not enthusiastic.
S - Specific. Consent must be specific. If you agree to sex on a Monday, that doesn't mean you also consent to sex on a Tuesday. If you consent to taking things slowly, but instead he is rough and moves quickly, that is not consent.

I know it sounds complicated, but in your case it's pretty simple. It doesn't matter if you agreed to have sex with him, because you agreed only to have protected sex with him. Consent has to be specific. You didn't consent to unprotected sex, and sex without consent is always rape.

You've done the smart thing by getting tested. Please stay away from this man. If he's violated your trust once, he will do it again. 

If you want to, you can get support in reporting this to the police, there are lots of charities who provide guidance to people who have been assaulted. It is completely your choice.

I am so sorry that this happened to you. It was not your fault. Your feelings are completely valid. Things will get better.

title: Unpopular Opinion: I'm tired of hearing the whole "it's not your job to teach someone about XYZ"...
body:
I realize this will likely not be a popular post based on the number of times I see this phrase in the comments on this particular sub but I still wanted to share this, maybe controversial but ultimately, alternative view/thought process.

I hate willful ignorance probably more than anything, but being *"willfully ignorant of"* & just being *"ignorant of"* are different things. title: Was it rape?
body: I kind of just recently acknowledged an event happened that I think falls under the umbrella of rape, but it feels too extreme of a classification. For context, I was 15 years old when I began dating my first boyfriend. He was one of the most amazing people who could make me laugh and would listen to me whenever I had a family issue, although in hindsight I really do think that I only began dating him because he prioritized me in a way that my dad refused to. Despite how kind he was, he did have a bad habit of pressuring me often into things I wasn’t quite comfortable with. For example, I had my first kiss with him about 3 months after we began dating, which was a direct effect of him asking over and over again over a span of weeks. I will admit I’m a bad people-pleaser, and I felt very responsible for his happiness. Eventually after enough asking and me saying no, I caved. However, I realize that he should’ve never gone through with it, since he literally had to cover my eyes because I was so terrified and frozen. The pressuring and guilting continued for months regarding more significant actions, which I always eventually caved in. The biggest problem was him continuing to ask me on a frequent basis, and then acting completely defeated after I would say no. He would often complain about not feeling “satisfied” in our relationship because of these refusals, which I would take on completely through guilt. However, one thing that I refused to cave on was sex. It was already a taboo topic for me, but I was 15 and didn’t feel ready for it. I had expressed for months that it wasn’t something I would even be willing to consider until I was 18. I have found journals from that time, though, that was trying to plead when he would speak of unhappiness and the possibility of breaking up because of it, saying “I’ve though about trying to comply so that he is happy”. Despite this, I am positive my boundaries were very clear. In May of the following year, he ended up breaking up with me because I refused to have sex with him. He soon returned and said it was the worst mistake he made, although it was still something he would continue to ask about. Then, two weeks later on my 16th birthday, we were in my room, and he was pressing me again. I really felt responsible for his happiness, so, stupidly, I consented to him rubbing down on the vulva, although stated that I wasn’t consenting to sex. Suddenly, as I was pressed against the bed frame, I felt him begin to push inside, which sent a surge of panic through me. I quickly began repeating “no no no” in a distressed manner, and I felt him continue to push inside. What I do remember, though, is that he never pushed all the way in, which makes me question the validity of the occasion. I regained control of my body and pushed him off of me. I began sobbing and curled up in a ball, and he came over immediately to apologize and ask if I was okay. I guess I didn’t really question the occasion and shrugged it off as miscommunication, although it always bugged me in the back of my head. After that, I took on sex as my responsibility in our relationship, as he would typically complain about it being too long since we had engaged in that. That being said, it would often be about 4-5 times a week. He often guilted me into it, and I felt as though I became somebody only useful for sex. Fast forward to January of the next year, and my dad found out about the whole situation. This acted as a catalyst for me to begin questioning the circumstances of the situation, and open it up to the possibility of sexual assault. I confronted him about it, and he at first told me that he didn’t realize he was inside and that he didn’t remember me saying no. However, I didn’t feel as though the “no” was relevant because I very clearly never gave him consent and was obviously distressed. Also, I had made it clear for months that I wouldn’t consent to this. It felt very frustrated because I didn’t want to chalk up something that felt very violating to just a miscommunication or “gray area”. After about 2 hours of talking, he finally admitted that in the moment he was just eager to get the opportunity, was prioritizing and focusing on himself and his own wants, and was ignoring me and what I was saying. This situation has caused significant disruption to my life, resulting in panic attacks and a lot of shame. I feel disgusting for it happening and a lot of self-blame. I feel like I let it get to that point by consenting to lesser things. I should’ve fought back more physically or yelled no louder. Maybe I just want to be a victim. He’s a good person and cared about me, and I don’t think it was out of malicious intent. But I do know that he forced himself inside me on my birthday without my consent, regardless of whether he remembers me saying no. I didn’t give me that respect, nor did he give me respect in the months previous with other boundaries. The other previous actions I did ultimately consent to, so I don’t have anyone else to blame but me. I was just coerced and manipulated, but I said yes. Sex, I never said yes to. But I still love him and I’m not going to press charges. I just feel like I could’ve done more and it wasn’t that bad. If it is rape, it falls in the lesser end of the spectrum because it wasn’t violent or while I was unconscious. I just want my panic and feelings of violation and disgust and shame to be valid. Can someone give me their opinions on what happened?

title: Unpopular Opinion: I'm tired of hearing the whole "it's not your job to teach someone about XYZ"...
body:
I realize this will likely not be a popular post based on the number of times I see this phrase in the comments on this particular sub but I still wanted to share this, maybe controversial but ultimately, alternative view/thought process.

I hate willful ignorance probably more than anything, but being *"willfully ignorant of"* & just being *"ignorant of"* are different things. Some people grow up sheltered, privileged, unaware of the existence of prejudice or malice - They are ignorant in the sense that they don't yet know that another view, or experience, is different than their own. Willful ignorance however, is when someone knows those things but chooses to dismiss or ignore them altogether to remain close-minded. So when I see people say things like "It's not your job to teach your boyfriend about sexism" or "it's not your job to explain what privilege is to others" it bothers me because we were all ignorant of something, sometime in our life & if someone didn't teach us, we'd never know. I think it is our job, especially with those we're close with to at least try and help them understand something they may not be aware of. Now if the person does know & chooses to keep recognizing ONLY their experience, that's willful ignorance and it's not your job to "convince them" something merits consideration.

As an example, when I was around 18-19 I worked as a server/bartender and became good friends with this guy named Rocky. I should explain that I went to a small school (200 kids maybe) and it was almost completely white and I honestly had very little interaction with people from other races - which sucks btw - so there were a lot of things I didn't understand about the POC experience. Was I aware of racism? Yes, of course this is America but I didn't really understand the real life implications or experience of POC. Rocky was a black guy, and being friends with him was easy but I was constantly learning from him about his experience. One night we're working behind the bar together & this group comes in, they start ordering drinks but I also notice they keep calling Rocky, Tyrone. Now in my head I'm thinking they just can't see his name tag or maybe they misheard him, I'll correct them but when I do the guy just says "oh he your boyfriend or something?" I just said no, he's my friend & his name is Rocky but I realized this guy was *only* planning to respect Rocky if we were dating.

Later when the bar closed I asked Rocky what was up because I could see he was down. He explained how often that shit happened, where they'd use a "stereotypical black guy name" in a pejorative way unless a white person was around to give him "legitimacy". He told me about how these little things (micro-aggressions) had happened his whole life, how it affected him & his brothers. Rocky didn't have to share that with me, he could have taken the "it's not my job to explain racism to you" route but then I might never have understood micro-aggressions in the way I do now.

Yes I agree to some degree that it's every individuals responsibility to learn about how their experiences aren't shared by all, but I also think it's every one's job to help others who want to learn, understand them better. We don't all have the same experience and we don't all learn things at the same time so if it's not our job to help others understand, then whose job is it?

Really I guess this long rant is because I want to see more people sharing their experiences so we can understand them better and learn how to be better allies to each other. It would be amazing if people didn't need experiences like mine with Rocky to understand the weight of some things, but often it's just a lack of exposure and not willful ignorance.

**ETA: Due to the volume of messages attacking me, my husband and whatever minor semantics bothered people about this observation and request for more understanding I'm taking a break from the sub for a while. It's clear that while many are interested in using this forum for helping others understand women's perspectives, others are intent on using it to disparage others for simply not knowing something. I stand behind my statements.**

I’m sorry you’re going through this ❤️

While I understand why you feel it might be easier to just “go with it” instead of telling him the truth and risk disappointing him I think that would be a bad idea. You could dissociate which might leave him feeling like he did something wrong or wasn’t good enough. You might get emotional or cry during or afterwards (I’ve been there and it’s embarrassing in the moment, but easier to manage when my partner knows ahead of time that it has nothing to do with them). You can also let him know what might be comforting to you ahead of time if you do get emotional or dissociate if you do choose to have sex. Sometimes it can be difficult to explain in the moment so I’ve found that my partner can help more when I tell him beforehand. 

That’s just my thought on it but you know what’s best for you so trust yourself ❤️

title: Unpopular Opinion: I'm tired of hearing the whole "it's not your job to teach someone about XYZ"...
body:
I realize this will likely not be a popular post based on the number of times I see this phrase in the comments on this particular sub but I still wanted to share this, maybe controversial but ultimately, alternative view/thought process.

I hate willful ignorance probably more than anything, but being *"willfully ignorant of"* & just being *"ignorant of"* are different things. Some people grow up sheltered, privileged, unaware of the existence of prejudice or malice - They are ignorant in the sense that they don't yet know that another view, or experience, is different than their own. Willful ignorance however, is when someone knows those things but chooses to dismiss or ignore them altogether to remain close-minded. So when I see people say things like "It's not your job to teach your boyfriend about sexism" or "it's not your job to explain what privilege is to others" it bothers me because we were all ignorant of something, sometime in our life & if someone didn't teach us, we'd never know. I think it is our job, especially with those we're close with to at least try and help them understand something they may not be aware of. Now if the person does know & chooses to keep recognizing ONLY their experience, that's willful ignorance and it's not your job to "convince them" something merits consideration.

As an example, when I was around 18-19 I worked as a server/bartender and became good friends with this guy named Rocky. I should explain that I went to a small school (200 kids maybe) and it was almost completely white and I honestly had very little interaction with people from other races - which sucks btw - so there were a lot of things I didn't understand about the POC experience. Was I aware of racism? Yes, of course this is America but I didn't really understand the real life implications or experience of POC. Rocky was a black guy, and being friends with him was easy but I was constantly learning from him about his experience. One night we're working behind the bar together & this group comes in, they start ordering drinks but I also notice they keep calling Rocky, Tyrone. Now in my head I'm thinking they just can't see his name tag or maybe they misheard him, I'll correct them but when I do the guy just says "oh he your boyfriend or something?" I just said no, he's my friend & his name is Rocky but I realized this guy was *only* planning to respect Rocky if we were dating.

Later when the bar closed I asked Rocky what was up because I could see he was down. He explained how often that shit happened, where they'd use a "stereotypical black guy name" in a pejorative way unless a white person was around to give him "legitimacy". He told me about how these little things (micro-aggressions) had happened his whole life, how it affected him & his brothers. Rocky didn't have to share that with me, he could have taken the "it's not my job to explain racism to you" route but then I might never have understood micro-aggressions in the way I do now.

Yes I agree to some degree that it's every individuals responsibility to learn about how their experiences aren't shared by all, but I also think it's every one's job to help others who want to learn, understand them better. We don't all have the same experience and we don't all learn things at the same time so if it's not our job to help others understand, then whose job is it?

Really I guess this long rant is because I want to see more people sharing their experiences so we can understand them better and learn how to be better allies to each other. It would be amazing if people didn't need experiences like mine with Rocky to understand the weight of some things, but often it's just a lack of exposure and not willful ignorance.

**ETA: Due to the volume of messages attacking me, my husband and whatever minor semantics bothered people about this observation and request for more understanding I'm taking a break from the sub for a while. It's clear that while many are interested in using this forum for helping others understand women's perspectives, others are intent on using it to disparage others for simply not knowing something. I stand behind my statements.**

parent_comment:
>Unpopular Opinion: I'm tired of hearing the whole "it's not your job to teach someone about XYZ"...

This is your title. *You* may feel that it is your job, but to tell others that are being hurt and victimized that they simply must do more is absolutely harmful and wrong. It is NOT their job. That really should be the takeaway here.

It is *empowering* for many people to be told they can step back. That *their* health, both physical and mental, is important and they can choose that. We have been conditioned to take on more emotional labor than can be supported and getting supported that that does not make you weak, that does not mean you are not doing enough, that you are not failing is absolutely a positive thing. Telling someone hurting that you are tired of them not educating because *you* choose to take on that burden with this one thing is destructive and not allyship. The worst kind of ally actually.

This is exactly what we are talking about here. Lots of people doing the emotional labor of telling you *why* we may say that and the effects constantly educating does, and you are saying that is not enough because the ignorant need educating and it is their duty to educate them. This is the educational opportunity you are talking about and yet when it is *your* behavior and *your* words being challenged, look what happened. You are not taking this on. You are not understanding. And that really is the outcome of most times educating on why something is hurtful. It is the arguing that you *should* do it anyway because the other person doesn't see the issue with it.

If your post title had been "I am really tired of how most people take being educated on where they are wrong and how that discourages others from speaking up and educating" that would be wonderful! It is understanding. It is putting the focus not on your feelings but on the feelings of those actually being hurt. If your post body related that story of your coworker and then ended with saying how you are committing to taking on some of his burden by using every chance you can to call out racists and educate them, that would be wonderful!

But you didn't. And that is exactly why so many simply don't engage. That is why ignorance continues because even when we try, we aren't doing enough. Even when we lend emotional support to someone to let them know that they can prioritize their own health, we are told that those in the wrong are tired of not being taught. What you do with this educational opportunity is up to you. But understand it will show everyone what happens when you engage and try to educate.

I was already turned on, and I still was aroused, so I went with it. I didn't say anything. He still did not ask. We continued to have rough sex, which I really enjoyed and actively participated in.

But then I just continued on and decided to have sex and go with my feelings of arousal because the decision to have sex was already made for me.

He's a good person, and I'm not saying any of this to paint a bad image of him. I'm just really confused, and I'm not even sure if I should talk to him about this, or (if I do) how I should go about doing so.

Thanks in advance for reading this, and offering your opinions everyone. <3
